{"parentUuid":"64585c80-665a-4493-9d7d-702045d95782","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"dab45f80-42a3-444d-8092-be343cf2ed99","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Hd8316WR1LY62qnTVMdANF","type":"tool_result","content":"1\tVocabulary follows `CONTEXT.md`. Where the course manual says **post**, this spec says **Guide**.\n2\t\n3\t## Problem Statement\n4\t\n5\tGuides for The Bazaar (大巴扎) in the Chinese-speaking community exist only as Bilibili videos and live streams. Most of them are an up主 talking over a PowerPoint. That fails the people who use them:\n6\t\n7\t- **Readers** can't read a guide in a few spare minutes, or when they can't turn the sound on. They can't jump straight to the end-game build (终局阵容) for a given Hero, and they can't tell whether a video still applies after a balance patch. Patches come about twice a month.\n8\t- **Streamers and invited writers** already have the material (screenshots of lineups and decks, plus an explanation). They have nowhere to publish it as text, organized so a Reader can find it by Hero, Patch or Author.\n9\t- **The streamers who would run a site** are good at managing fan groups but not comfortable with computers. They need a strict line between themselves and invited writers. Nothing reaches the public site until an Admin has reviewed it.\n10\t\n11\t## Solution\n12\t\n13\t**大巴扎攻略站** is a small CMS with an admin console and a static public site.\n14\t\n15\t- Editors write Guides in Markdown. Each Guide has exactly one Hero and one Patch, uploaded screenshots, and a Chinese text plus an optional English text.\n16\t- Editors Submit Guides for review. Admins Publish them, or Return them with Review notes.\n17\t- An Admin clicks **更新网站** (Site build) to regenerate the public site and put it on GitHub Pages.\n18\t- Readers browse Guides by Hero (grouped by Patch, newest first) or by Author. They can switch the whole site between Chinese and English, and they see the Current Patch in the header.\n19\t- Game names (Heroes, Items, Skills and the rest) always appear as the game's Official names, in the Reader's language.\n20\t\n21\t### The 7 required capabilities, for this client\n22\t\n23\t1. **Login.** Admins and Editors sign in with email and password, and sign out. Passwords are hashed with argon2 and never stored or logged in plain text. Deactivated accounts can't log in. An account created by an Admin starts with a temporary password, and on first login the person sets their own password and Display name.\n24\t2. **Two roles.** **Admin** (管理员): a streamer who runs the site, reviews and Publishes everyone's Guides, and manages users, Pages, Tournament items, Game Terms and Patches. **Editor** (编辑): an invited writer who writes their own Guides and Submits them. An Editor can never Publish, Return, see other people's unpublished Guides, or manage users.\n25\t3. **Posts = Guides.** Each Guide has full create, read, update and delete:\n26\t   - **Fields:** a title and a Markdown body per language, a slug, a Hero, a Patch, a status (Draft / Submitted / Published), the Author, and timestamps.\n27\t   - **Changing a Published Guide:** goes through a Revision, so the live Guide stays up until the change is approved.\n28\t   - **Deleting:** sends the Guide to the Trash.\n29\t4. **Pages.** Admins write Pages (About 关于) with the same fields minus Hero and Patch. Published Pages appear in the public navigation. Tournament announcements and recaps are a small Admin-only list under the 锦标赛 menu.\n30\t5. **Admin console.** A role-aware dashboard with counts (待审核, Returned, my Drafts, changes not yet on the site) and a content list filterable by status, Hero, Author, Patch and language. The Markdown editor has a preview that shows the Guide as Readers will see it, with warnings for unknown Game Terms and nicknames.\n31\t6. **User management (Admin only).** A Users page where Admins can:\n32\t   - create accounts and change roles,\n33\t   - apply or lift a Submission ban,\n34\t   - deactivate or reactivate accounts,\n35\t   - reset passwords.\n36\t\n37\t   Deactivated users can't log in. Admins can't deactivate or demote themselves, and the last active Admin can never be removed.\n38\t7. **Public site and Site build.**\n39\t   - Only Published content is written, with Markdown sanitized.\n40\t   - The navigation is 攻略 and 锦标赛 plus the Published Pages.\n41\t   - The site is built as Chinese and English versions with relative paths only.\n42\t   - The Site build (`cms publish` plus deploy, or the 更新网站 button) is the only step that changes what Readers see.\n43\t\n44\t## User Stories\n45\t\n46\t### Accounts and login\n47\t\n48\t1. As an Admin, I want to sign in with my email and password, so that only I can use my Admin powers.\n49\t2. As an Editor, I want to sign in with my email and password, so that I can work on my Guides.\n50\t3. As an Admin or Editor, I want to sign out, so that nobody else at this computer can act as me.\n51\t4. As an Admin, I want passwords stored only as argon2 hashes, so that a leaked database doesn't leak anyone's password.\n52\t5. As a new Editor, I want to set my own password on first login, so that the temporary password the Admin chose stops working.\n53\t6. As a new Editor, I want to choose my own Display name (my Bilibili name) on first login, so that Readers recognize me.\n54\t7. As an Editor, I want to change my Display name later in my profile, so that I can follow a rename on Bilibili.\n55\t8. As an Author, I want my Display name to be unique on the site, so that Readers never confuse me with another writer.\n56\t9. As an Author, I want my login email never shown on the public site, so that strangers can't use it to try to log in as me.\n57\t10. As a Deactivated user, I want a clear \"account deactivated\" message when I try to log in, so that I know to contact an Admin rather than retry.\n58\t11. As an Admin, I want every form that changes something to carry a CSRF token, so that a malicious link can't act on my behalf.\n59\t\n60\t### Writing Guides\n61\t\n62\t12. As an Editor, I want to create a Guide with a Chinese title and Markdown body, so that I can turn my PowerPoint into a readable text.\n63\t13. As an Editor, I want to optionally add an English title and body, so that English-speaking players can read my Guide too.\n64\t14. As an Editor, I want to pick the Hero from a list of Official names, so that my Guide lands under the right Hero and never under a nickname.\n65\t15. As an Editor, I want to pick the Patch from a list showing `6.7（当前版本）` and the two Patches before it, with the Current Patch preselected, so that I don't have to type or guess the version.\n66\t16. As an Editor, I want to save a Draft and come back later, so that I can write a long Guide over several sittings.\n67\t17. As an Editor, I want to upload screenshots of lineups and decks into my Guide, so that the pictures from my PowerPoint go straight into the text.\n68\t18. As an Editor, I want to give each image an optional short description (alt text), so that Readers using screen readers, or whose images fail to load, still know what the picture shows.\n69\t19. As an Editor, I want to choose which uploaded image is the Guide's cover, defaulting to the first, so that my Guide looks right in the lists.\n70\t20. As an Editor, I want to use one uploaded image in both my Chinese and my English text, so that I don't upload it twice.\n71\t21. As an Editor, I want to mark a Game Term in my text as `[[瓦妮莎]]` or `[[Vanessa]]`, so that it shows as the Official name in whichever language the Reader is using.\n72\t22. As an Editor, I want the preview to warn me about a `[[…]]` that matches no Game Term, so that I can fix typos before an Admin sees them.\n73\t23. As an Editor, I want the preview to warn me when I've used a known nickname (such as 瓦姐) unmarked, so that I can replace it with the Official name.\n74\t24. As an Editor, I want the preview to show my Guide as Readers will see it, so that I know the screenshots and layout come out right.\n75\t25. As an Editor, I want to Submit (提交审核) a finished Guide, so that it goes to the Admins' review queue.\n76\t26. As an Editor, I want to be stopped from Submitting a Guide with no Chinese text, so that I don't send something that can't be Published.\n77\t27. As an Editor, I want the Submit button never to be labelled 发布, so that I'm not misled into thinking my Guide is live.\n78\t28. As an Editor, I want to see only my own Guides in the console, so that the list is about my work.\n79\t29. As an Editor, I want to edit my own Draft and Submitted Guides, so that I can fix something I noticed after Submitting.\n80\t\n81\t### Review\n82\t\n83\t30. As an Admin, I want a 待审核 count and queue on my dashboard, so that I never forget Guides waiting for me.\n84\t31. As an Admin, I want to read a Submitted Guide in the same preview Readers will get, so that I review exactly what would be Published.\n85\t32. As an Admin, I want to Publish a Submitted Guide, so that it goes on the site at the next Site build.\n86\t33. As an Admin, I want to Return a Submitted Guide with one or more Review notes, each quoting a passage and giving advice, so that the Editor knows exactly what to fix and why.\n87\t34. As an Editor, I want a badge on my dashboard when a Guide is Returned, so that I notice it without checking every Guide.\n88\t35. As an Editor, I want to see the Review notes at the top of my Returned Draft, with quoted passages that are still in the text highlighted in the preview, so that I can find each problem quickly.\n89\t36. As an Editor, I want to fix a Returned Guide and Submit it again, so that it can still be Published.\n90\t37. As an Admin, I want earlier Review notes kept with the Guide, so that I can see its history if it goes back and forth.\n91\t38. As an Admin, I want to fix small things myself and Publish directly, so that a typo doesn't cost a full round trip.\n92\t39. As an Admin, I want to change any Guide's Hero, so that I can fix a Guide filed under the wrong Hero.\n93\t40. As an Admin, I want to write and Publish my own Guides without review, so that streamers who run the site aren't slowed down.\n94\t\n95\t### Revisions, Unpublish, deletion\n96\t\n97\t41. As an Editor, I want to open a Revision on my Published Guide, so that I can update it for a new Patch while the old version stays on the site.\n98\t42. As an Editor, I want to save a Revision as a Draft and Submit it later, so that a big update can take several sittings.\n99\t43. As an Editor, I want my Revision to be able to change the Patch, so that a 6.7 Guide updated for 6.8 moves to the 6.8 group on its Hero's page.\n100\t44. As an Editor, I want an approved Revision to replace the old content completely, so that Readers only ever see the current version.\n101\t45. As an Admin, I want to Publish or Return a Revision just like a new Guide, so that review works the same either way.\n102\t46. As an Editor, I want a Returned Revision to leave my live Guide untouched, so that a rejected update never takes my Guide down.\n103\t47. As an Editor, I want at most one open Revision per Guide, so that there's never confusion about which change is pending.\n104\t48. As an Admin, I want my own edits to a Published Guide to take effect immediately, so that I don't have to review myself.\n105\t49. As a Reader, I want to see when a Guide was last updated (更新于), so that I can judge how fresh it is.\n106\t50. As an Admin, I want to Unpublish (撤下) a Guide with an optional Review note, so that I can take down a misleading Guide without destroying the Author's work.\n107\t51. As an Editor, I want an Unpublished Guide to come back to me as a Draft, so that I can fix it and Submit again.\n108\t52. As an Editor, I want to delete my own Guides, including Published ones, so that I stay in control of my work.\n109\t53. As an Editor, I want a confirmation before deleting, so that a misclick doesn't remove a Guide.\n110\t54. As an Admin, I want deleted Guides to go to a Trash only Admins can see, so that an accidental deletion can be undone.\n111\t55. As an Admin, I want to restore a Guide from the Trash, so that it returns to its Author in the state it was in.\n112\t56. As an Admin, I want to delete a Guide from the Trash for good, together with its images, so that the Trash doesn't grow forever.\n113\t57. As an Admin, I want any Guide in the Trash never to appear on the site, so that deleting a Guide always takes it down at the next Site build.\n114\t\n115\t### Game Terms and Patches\n116\t\n117\t58. As an Admin, I want to manage Game Terms of seven kinds (Hero, Item, Skill, Enchantment, Monster, Merchant, Event), each with its official Chinese and English name, so that the site always uses Official names.\n118\t59. As an Admin, I want to import Game Terms from a CSV file, so that thousands of Items and Skills don't have to be typed by hand.\n119\t60. As an Admin, I want CSV rows missing either Official name rejected with a clear per-row message, so that half-filled terms never get in.\n120\t61. As an Admin, I want to see what an import will add or change before it is saved, so that a bad CSV doesn't corrupt the term list.\n121\t62. As an Admin, I want to record known nicknames against a Game Term, so that the editor preview can warn Editors who use them.\n122\t63. As an Admin, I want each Hero to have a URL slug derived from its English Official name, so that Hero pages have clean addresses.\n123\t64. As an Admin, I want to add a new Patch, which becomes the Current Patch, so that a balance patch takes one action on my side.\n124\t65. As a Reader, I want the Current Patch shown in the site header, so that I can compare it with each Guide's Patch myself.\n125\t66. As a Reader, I want no automatic \"outdated\" labels, so that a Guide written for 6.6 that is still valid isn't wrongly flagged.\n126\t\n127\t### Pages and Tournaments\n128\t\n129\t67. As an Admin, I want to write an About (关于) Page with a Chinese and an optional English version, so that Readers know who runs the site and how to contact us.\n130\t68. As an Admin, I want Published Pages to appear in the public navigation automatically, so that I don't have to edit menus by hand.\n131\t69. As an Admin, I want to post a Tournament announcement with the Tournament's date, Patch and optional cover, so that Readers learn about an upcoming in-game Tournament.\n132\t70. As an Admin, I want to post a Tournament recap as its own item, optionally linked to its announcement, so that past Tournaments stay on record.\n133\t71. As a Reader, I want the 锦标赛 section to list announcements and recaps newest first, each badged 预告 or 回顾, so that I can tell at a glance what each item is.\n134\t\n135\t### User management\n136\t\n137\t72. As an Admin, I want a Users page listing every account's Display name, role, state, Guide counts and last login, so that I can see who's active.\n138\t73. As an Admin, I want to create an Editor or Admin account with an email and temporary password, so that I can invite a writer.\n139\t74. As an Admin, I want to change a user's role, so that I can promote a trusted Editor.\n140\t75. As an Admin, I want to apply a Submission ban (禁止投稿) to an Editor, so that they can't Submit while their Published Guides stay up.\n141\t76. As a banned Editor, I want to see why I can't Submit, so that I'm not confused by a missing button.\n142\t77. As an Admin, I want to deactivate and reactivate accounts, so that someone who leaves can't log in but their Published Guides stay on the site.\n143\t78. As an Admin, I want to reset a user's password to a new temporary one, so that a writer who forgot theirs can get back in.\n144\t79. As an Admin, I want the console to stop me from deactivating or demoting myself, and from removing the last active Admin, so that the site can't be locked out.\n145\t80. As an Editor, I want every user-management page to refuse me, even if I type its address, so that the role split is real and not just hidden buttons.\n146\t\n147\t### Dashboard and content list\n148\t\n149\t81. As an Admin, I want my dashboard to show 待审核, total Guides by status, and \"N 项更改尚未更新到网站\", so that I know what needs my attention.\n150\t82. As an Editor, I want my dashboard to show my Drafts, my Submitted Guides and my Returned Guides, so that I know where my work stands.\n151\t83. As an Admin, I want to filter the content list by status, Hero, Author, Patch and language, so that I can find any Guide quickly.\n152\t84. As an Admin or Editor, I want a success or error message after every save, so that I'm never unsure whether something worked.\n153\t85. As an Admin or Editor, I want a console navigation that stays on every page, so that I don't get lost the way I did in WordPress.\n154\t86. As an Admin or Editor, I want every console label in Chinese, so that the tool feels like ours.\n155\t\n156\t### Site build and public site\n157\t\n158\t87. As an Admin, I want an 更新网站 button that runs the Site build and puts the site online, so that I never have to open a terminal.\n159\t88. As an Admin, I want a clear message if the Site build fails, such as a failed push, so that I know the site didn't update.\n160\t89. As a Reader, I want a home page showing the Current Patch, the newest Guides and a grid of Heroes, so that I can start browsing immediately.\n161\t90. As a Reader, I want a page per Hero listing its Guides grouped by Patch, newest first, so that I can find a build for my Hero on this Patch.\n162\t91. As a Reader, I want a page per Author listing all their Guides, so that I can follow writers I trust.\n163\t92. As a Reader, I want list items to show the cover image, title, Hero, Patch, Author and date, so that I can choose a Guide without opening each one.\n164\t93. As a Reader, I want a language switch at the top right that switches the whole site, so that I can read entirely in Chinese or entirely in English.\n165\t94. As a Reader, I want switching language on a Guide to take me to the same Guide in the other language, or to its Hero's page with a notice if it isn't available, so that the switch never leads nowhere.\n166\t95. As an English Reader, I want only Guides with English text listed on the English site, so that I never land on a page in a language I can't read.\n167\t96. As a Reader, I want Hero and Author pages to exist in both languages, with a \"No English guides yet\" notice when empty, so that every link works.\n168\t97. As a Reader, I want `[[Game Term]]` markers shown as the Official name in my language, so that Item and Skill names match what I see in game.\n169\t98. As a Reader, I want Guide addresses that stay the same after a Revision, such as `guides/vanessa-12/`, so that links shared in Bilibili comments keep working.\n170\t99. As a Reader, I want the site to work when served from a subfolder of GitHub Pages, so that every link and image loads.\n171\t100. As an Admin, I want Drafts, Submitted Guides, open Revisions and the Trash never to appear on the site, so that only reviewed work is public.\n172\t101. As a Reader, I want any script or unsafe HTML in a Guide stripped, so that a Guide can never attack my browser.\n173\t\n174\t### Stretch\n175\t\n176\t102. As an Admin, I want the console hosted somewhere Editors can reach from their own computers, behind the security gate (password from the environment, rate-limited login, HTTPS, no default accounts), so that writers across China can actually use it.\n177\t\n178\t## Implementation Decisions\n179\t\n180\t**Modules**\n181\t\n182\t- **Accounts.** Users, login and logout, sessions (signed cookies via itsdangerous), argon2 hashing, CSRF tokens on every state-changing form, first-login setup (password plus Display name), and account states (active / Submission ban / Deactivated).\n183\t  - Login is by email, matching the existing `client_as` test fixture. The Display name is separate, unique, and the only name shown publicly.\n184\t  - Roles are bundles of capabilities. Route code checks a capability, not a role name, so a rule can change without touching routes.\n185\t- **Guide workflow.** A deep module that owns every state change and its permission check: create, save, Submit, Publish, Return (with Review notes), Unpublish, open and Submit a Revision, delete to Trash, restore, delete for good. Its interface takes the acting user and the Guide, and either performs the change or refuses with a reason the console can show. No route changes Guide status directly.\n186\t  - Guide states: Draft → Submitted → Published, with Return and Unpublish leading back to Draft. \"In Trash\" is separate from status, so a restored Guide comes back exactly as it was.\n187\t  - A Revision is a pending copy of a Published Guide's editable fields (texts, Hero, Patch, images, cover), with its own Draft/Submitted state. There is at most one per Guide. Publishing it overwrites the Guide's fields and updates its timestamp. The old content isn't kept. Returning it leaves the Guide untouched.\n188\t  - Admin edits to a Published Guide apply directly with no Revision.\n189\t  - Submit requires Chinese text and is refused under a Submission ban.\n190\t  - Review notes belong to the Guide and each stores a quoted passage, the advice, the Admin, and the time. They are kept across rounds.\n191\t- **Content.**\n192\t  - Guides have per-language title and body (Chinese required to Submit, English optional), a Hero, a Patch, the Author, a cover image, and created/updated/published timestamps.\n193\t  - Pages have per-language text, a status (Draft/Published) and an Admin-set ASCII slug. Only Admins can manage them, with no review.\n194\t  - Tournament items are of kind announcement or recap, with per-language text, a Tournament date, a Patch, an optional cover, an optional link from recap to announcement, and a Draft/Published status. Only Admins can manage them.\n195\t- **Game Terms and Patches.**\n196\t  - **Game Terms:** each has one of the seven kinds, both Official names (both required), and an optional list of nicknames. Heroes also have a URL slug from the English name.\n197\t  - **CSV import:** uses Python's standard library, previews the changes, and rejects rows per row with a reason.\n198\t  - **Patches:** a Patch is an ordered list entry, and the newest one is the Current Patch. The Guide form offers the Current Patch and the two before it, and still shows a Guide's existing older Patch.\n199\t- **Markdown rendering.** One function used by both the editor preview and the Site build:\n200\t  1. Markdown is turned into HTML with markdown-it-py.\n201\t  2. `[[term]]` markers become the Official name in the target language, matched by either language's name, and styled as a term.\n202\t  3. The HTML is sanitized with nh3.\n203\t\n204\t  The same pass returns warnings (unknown terms, unmarked nicknames) for the preview. Warnings never block Submit. Review notes' quoted passages are highlighted in the preview only, never on the public site.\n205\t- **Media.**\n206\t  - **Accepted files:** PNG, JPG, WebP and GIF only (no SVG), checked by content as well as extension. 5 MB maximum each.\n207\t  - **Storage:** server-generated filenames. Images are owned by a Guide (or a Tournament item) and usable from either language's text. Each image has optional per-language alt text.\n208\t  - **Site build and deletion:** images are copied into the site output during the Site build, and deleted with their owner when it is deleted for good.\n209\t- **Site build.** It is an extension of the existing `render_site(out)`.\n210\t  - **Output:** two trees, `zh/` and `en/`. The root `index.html` sends Readers to `zh/`.\n211\t  - **Pages written per language:** the home page, a Guides index, one page per Hero, one per Author with at least one Published Guide, one per Guide, the Tournaments list and each item, and each Published Page.\n212\t  - **Language filter:** the English tree includes only items with English text. Hero and Author pages exist in both trees, with an empty notice when needed.\n213\t  - **Links:** every link is relative, computed from each page's depth. The language switch links to the same page in the other tree, or falls back to the Hero page with a notice.\n214\t  - **What is excluded:** only Published, non-Trash content is read, so open Revisions are never seen.\n215\t  - **Deploy:** the existing `cms deploy` (ghp-import) puts the site online. The console's 更新网站 button runs render plus deploy and shows the result. The CLI commands stay as they are.\n216\t  - The dashboard's \"changes not yet on the site\" count compares content change times with the last successful Site build.\n217\t- **URLs.**\n218\t  - **Guides:** `guides/<hero-slug>-<id>/`. The slug is generated on creation, Admins can edit it, and it is unique. It never changes on its own with a title or Revision.\n219\t  - **Other pages:** Heroes `heroes/<slug>/`, Authors `authors/<id>/` (never the email), Tournament items `tournaments/<id>/`, Pages `<page-slug>/`.\n220\t- **Admin console.** Server-rendered Jinja templates with Chinese labels throughout:\n221\t  - a role-aware dashboard,\n222\t  - the filterable content list,\n223\t  - the Guide editor with preview, image upload, cover choice and alt text,\n224\t  - a review screen with a Review note builder,\n225\t  - the Users page, the Trash, Game Terms with CSV import, and Patches.\n226\t\n227\t  Navigation stays on every page, and every save shows a success or error message.\n228\t- **Storage.** SQLite at `CMS_DATABASE`. The schema is created on startup. `scripts/seed_demo.py` creates one Admin and one Editor from environment passwords, plus demo Heroes, Patches, Game Terms, Guides in every status, a Page and Tournament items.\n229\t- **Architecture.** ADR-001 and ADR-002 stand for all core work. The hosted console is a stretch ticket. When it starts, ADR-003 will supersede ADR-001 for the console, and the `CLAUDE.md` \"never on the public internet\" rule will be updated in the same change. Until then the console runs on one machine. That is a known gap for a real multi-author deployment.\n230\t\n231\t## Testing Decisions\n232\t\n233\t- **A good test** drives the system the way a user does and checks what a user would see: an HTTP response, a redirect, a page's text, or a file in the built site. Tests never inspect database rows or call private helpers, so the internals can be rebuilt without rewriting tests. Test names use the `CONTEXT.md` vocabulary (e.g. `test_editor_cannot_publish_a_submitted_guide`).\n234\t- **Seam 1: the admin console over HTTP.** This uses the existing `client` and `client_as(role)` fixtures. It covers login and logout, account states, CSRF rejection, every permission rule (including Editors refused on Admin routes by URL), the full Guide workflow, Revisions, Review notes, Trash, Submission bans, user management guards, Game Term CSV import, Patch handling, image upload validation, and preview warnings.\n235\t- **Seam 2: the Site build.** This uses the existing `render_site(out)` into a temporary folder, after content is set up through Seam 1. It covers:\n236\t  - Published-only output: no Drafts, Submitted Guides, open Revisions or Trash.\n237\t  - Relative paths only, across every generated page.\n238\t  - Sanitized Markdown: injected script is stripped.\n239\t  - `[[term]]` rendering per language.\n240\t  - The English tree excluding Chinese-only items.\n241\t  - Hero pages grouped by Patch.\n242\t  - Author pages using Display names only.\n243\t  - Navigation built from Published Pages.\n244\t  - Images copied, with alt text.\n245\t- **Isolation.** Each test gets a fresh SQLite database through `CMS_DATABASE` in a temporary folder, seeded with the `DEMO_USERS` from the test fixtures.\n246\t- **Prior art:** `tests/test_t00.py` (HTTP and `render_site` checks, the relative-path assertion) and `tests/conftest.py` (`client_as`). The T00 tests must keep passing.\n247\t- **Deploy** (the git push) isn't tested automatically. The button's handling of success and failure is tested with the push step replaced.\n248\t\n249\t## Out of Scope\n250\t\n251\t- Comments and discussion. These stay on Bilibili.\n252\t- Reader accounts.\n253\t- Site search. Browsing by Hero, Author and Patch covers the need on a static site.\n254\t- Translation inside the CMS (machine or AI). Writers bring their own English text.\n255\t- A card database or patch-notes section. The community wiki already covers it.\n256\t- Automatic \"outdated\" labels on Guides.\n257\t- Revision history and rollback. An approved Revision replaces the old content.\n258\t- Scheduled publishing.\n259\t- Streamer announcements as a content type.\n260\t- Multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, and WYSIWYG editors (excluded by the manual).\n261\t- Hosting the console in core. It is the last stretch ticket only.\n262\t\n263\t## Further Notes\n264\t\n265\t- **Stretch tickets planned:** (1) image uploads with alt text, which the client needs and the rubric counts as \"Media uploads with alt text\"; (2) the hosted admin console behind the security gate, done last, with ADR-003.\n266\t- **Known gap until the hosted console exists:** Editors on their own computers can't reach a console running on one Admin's machine. In the meantime every feature is built as if the console were shared: real logins, roles, CSRF, and no default accounts.\n267\t- Because of ADR-001, Publishing doesn't change the public site by itself. follows `CONTEXT.md`. Where the course manual says **post**, this spec says **Guide**.\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nGuides for The Bazaar (大巴扎) in the Chinese-speaking community exist only as Bilibili videos and live streams. Most of them are an up主 talking over a PowerPoint. That fails the people who use them:\n\n- **Readers** can't read a guide in a few spare minutes, or when they can't turn the sound on. They can't jump straight to the end-game build (终局阵容) for a given Hero, and they can't tell whether a video still applies after a balance patch. Patches come about twice a month.\n- **Streamers and invited writers** already have the material (screenshots of lineups and decks, plus an explanation). They have nowhere to publish it as text, organized so a Reader can find it by Hero, Patch or Author.\n- **The streamers who would run a site** are good at managing fan groups but not comfortable with computers. They need a strict line between themselves and invited writers. Nothing reaches the public site until an Admin has reviewed it.\n\n## Solution\n\n**大巴扎攻略站** is a small CMS with an admin console and a static public site.\n\n- Editors write Guides in Markdown. Each Guide has exactly one Hero and one Patch, uploaded screenshots, and a Chinese text plus an optional English text.\n- Editors Submit Guides for review. Admins Publish them, or Return them with Review notes.\n- An Admin clicks **更新网站** (Site build) to regenerate the public site and put it on GitHub Pages.\n- Readers browse Guides by Hero (grouped by Patch, newest first) or by Author. They can switch the whole site between Chinese and English, and they see the Current Patch in the header.\n- Game names (Heroes, Items, Skills and the rest) always appear as the game's Official names, in the Reader's language.\n\n### The 7 required capabilities, for this client\n\n1. **Login.** Admins and Editors sign in with email and password, and sign out. Passwords are hashed with argon2 and never stored or logged in plain text. Deactivated accounts can't log in. An account created by an Admin starts with a temporary password, and on first login the person sets their own password and Display name.\n2. **Two roles.** **Admin** (管理员): a streamer who runs the site, reviews and Publishes everyone's Guides, and manages users, Pages, Tournament items, Game Terms and Patches. **Editor** (编辑): an invited writer who writes their own Guides and Submits them. An Editor can never Publish, Return, see other people's unpublished Guides, or manage users.\n3. **Posts = Guides.** Each Guide has full create, read, update and delete:\n   - **Fields:** a title and a Markdown body per language, a slug, a Hero, a Patch, a status (Draft / Submitted / Published), the Author, and timestamps.\n   - **Changing a Published Guide:** goes through a Revision, so the live Guide stays up until the change is approved.\n   - **Deleting:** sends the Guide to the Trash.\n4. **Pages.** Admins write Pages (About 关于) with the same fields minus Hero and Patch. Published Pages appear in the public navigation. Tournament announcements and recaps are a small Admin-only list under the 锦标赛 menu.\n5. **Admin console.** A role-aware dashboard with counts (待审核, Returned, my Drafts, changes not yet on the site) and a content list filterable by status, Hero, Author, Patch and language. The Markdown editor has a preview that shows the Guide as Readers will see it, with warnings for unknown Game Terms and nicknames.\n6. **User management (Admin only).** A Users page where Admins can:\n   - create accounts and change roles,\n   - apply or lift a Submission ban,\n   - deactivate or reactivate accounts,\n   - reset passwords.\n\n   Deactivated users can't log in. Admins can't deactivate or demote themselves, and the last active Admin can never be removed.\n7. **Public site and Site build.**\n   - Only Published content is written, with Markdown sanitized.\n   - The navigation is 攻略 and 锦标赛 plus the Published Pages.\n   - The site is built as Chinese and English versions with relative paths only.\n   - The Site build (`cms publish` plus deploy, or the 更新网站 button) is the only step that changes what Readers see.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Accounts and login\n\n1. As an Admin, I want to sign in with my email and password, so that only I can use my Admin powers.\n2. As an Editor, I want to sign in with my email and password, so that I can work on my Guides.\n3. As an Admin or Editor, I want to sign out, so that nobody else at this computer can act as me.\n4. As an Admin, I want passwords stored only as argon2 hashes, so that a leaked database doesn't leak anyone's password.\n5. As a new Editor, I want to set my own password on first login, so that the temporary password the Admin chose stops working.\n6. As a new Editor, I want to choose my own Display name (my Bilibili name) on first login, so that Readers recognize me.\n7. As an Editor, I want to change my Display name later in my profile, so that I can follow a rename on Bilibili.\n8. As an Author, I want my Display name to be unique on the site, so that Readers never confuse me with another writer.\n9. As an Author, I want my login email never shown on the public site, so that strangers can't use it to try to log in as me.\n10. As a Deactivated user, I want a clear \"account deactivated\" message when I try to log in, so that I know to contact an Admin rather than retry.\n11. As an Admin, I want every form that changes something to carry a CSRF token, so that a malicious link can't act on my behalf.\n\n### Writing Guides\n\n12. As an Editor, I want to create a Guide with a Chinese title and Markdown body, so that I can turn my PowerPoint into a readable text.\n13. As an Editor, I want to optionally add an English title and body, so that English-speaking players can read my Guide too.\n14. As an Editor, I want to pick the Hero from a list of Official names, so that my Guide lands under the right Hero and never under a nickname.\n15. As an Editor, I want to pick the Patch from a list showing `6.7（当前版本）` and the two Patches before it, with the Current Patch preselected, so that I don't have to type or guess the version.\n16. As an Editor, I want to save a Draft and come back later, so that I can write a long Guide over several sittings.\n17. As an Editor, I want to upload screenshots of lineups and decks into my Guide, so that the pictures from my PowerPoint go straight into the text.\n18. As an Editor, I want to give each image an optional short description (alt text), so that Readers using screen readers, or whose images fail to load, still know what the picture shows.\n19. As an Editor, I want to choose which uploaded image is the Guide's cover, defaulting to the first, so that my Guide looks right in the lists.\n20. As an Editor, I want to use one uploaded image in both my Chinese and my English text, so that I don't upload it twice.\n21. As an Editor, I want to mark a Game Term in my text as `[[瓦妮莎]]` or `[[Vanessa]]`, so that it shows as the Official name in whichever language the Reader is using.\n22. As an Editor, I want the preview to warn me about a `[[…]]` that matches no Game Term, so that I can fix typos before an Admin sees them.\n23. As an Editor, I want the preview to warn me when I've used a known nickname (such as 瓦姐) unmarked, so that I can replace it with the Official name.\n24. As an Editor, I want the preview to show my Guide as Readers will see it, so that I know the screenshots and layout come out right.\n25. As an Editor, I want to Submit (提交审核) a finished Guide, so that it goes to the Admins' review queue.\n26. As an Editor, I want to be stopped from Submitting a Guide with no Chinese text, so that I don't send something that can't be Published.\n27. As an Editor, I want the Submit button never to be labelled 发布, so that I'm not misled into thinking my Guide is live.\n28. As an Editor, I want to see only my own Guides in the console, so that the list is about my work.\n29. As an Editor, I want to edit my own Draft and Submitted Guides, so that I can fix something I noticed after Submitting.\n\n### Review\n\n30. As an Admin, I want a 待审核 count and queue on my dashboard, so that I never forget Guides waiting for me.\n31. As an Admin, I want to read a Submitted Guide in the same preview Readers will get, so that I review exactly what would be Published.\n32. As an Admin, I want to Publish a Submitted Guide, so that it goes on the site at the next Site build.\n33. As an Admin, I want to Return a Submitted Guide with one or more Review notes, each quoting a passage and giving advice, so that the Editor knows exactly what to fix and why.\n34. As an Editor, I want a badge on my dashboard when a Guide is Returned, so that I notice it without checking every Guide.\n35. As an Editor, I want to see the Review notes at the top of my Returned Draft, with quoted passages that are still in the text highlighted in the preview, so that I can find each problem quickly.\n36. As an Editor, I want to fix a Returned Guide and Submit it again, so that it can still be Published.\n37. As an Admin, I want earlier Review notes kept with the Guide, so that I can see its history if it goes back and forth.\n38. As an Admin, I want to fix small things myself and Publish directly, so that a typo doesn't cost a full round trip.\n39. As an Admin, I want to change any Guide's Hero, so that I can fix a Guide filed under the wrong Hero.\n40. As an Admin, I want to write and Publish my own Guides without review, so that streamers who run the site aren't slowed down.\n\n### Revisions, Unpublish, deletion\n\n41. As an Editor, I want to open a Revision on my Published Guide, so that I can update it for a new Patch while the old version stays on the site.\n42. As an Editor, I want to save a Revision as a Draft and Submit it later, so that a big update can take several sittings.\n43. As an Editor, I want my Revision to be able to change the Patch, so that a 6.7 Guide updated for 6.8 moves to the 6.8 group on its Hero's page.\n44. As an Editor, I want an approved Revision to replace the old content completely, so that Readers only ever see the current version.\n45. As an Admin, I want to Publish or Return a Revision just like a new Guide, so that review works the same either way.\n46. As an Editor, I want a Returned Revision to leave my live Guide untouched, so that a rejected update never takes my Guide down.\n47. As an Editor, I want at most one open Revision per Guide, so that there's never confusion about which change is pending.\n48. As an Admin, I want my own edits to a Published Guide to take effect immediately, so that I don't have to review myself.\n49. As a Reader, I want to see when a Guide was last updated (更新于), so that I can judge how fresh it is.\n50. As an Admin, I want to Unpublish (撤下) a Guide with an optional Review note, so that I can take down a misleading Guide without destroying the Author's work.\n51. As an Editor, I want an Unpublished Guide to come back to me as a Draft, so that I can fix it and Submit again.\n52. As an Editor, I want to delete my own Guides, including Published ones, so that I stay in control of my work.\n53. As an Editor, I want a confirmation before deleting, so that a misclick doesn't remove a Guide.\n54. As an Admin, I want deleted Guides to go to a Trash only Admins can see, so that an accidental deletion can be undone.\n55. As an Admin, I want to restore a Guide from the Trash, so that it returns to its Author in the state it was in.\n56. As an Admin, I want to delete a Guide from the Trash for good, together with its images, so that the Trash doesn't grow forever.\n57. As an Admin, I want any Guide in the Trash never to appear on the site, so that deleting a Guide always takes it down at the next Site build.\n\n### Game Terms and Patches\n\n58. As an Admin, I want to manage Game Terms of seven kinds (Hero, Item, Skill, Enchantment, Monster, Merchant, Event), each with its official Chinese and English name, so that the site always uses Official names.\n59. As an Admin, I want to import Game Terms from a CSV file, so that thousands of Items and Skills don't have to be typed by hand.\n60. As an Admin, I want CSV rows missing either Official name rejected with a clear per-row message, so that half-filled terms never get in.\n61. As an Admin, I want to see what an import will add or change before it is saved, so that a bad CSV doesn't corrupt the term list.\n62. As an Admin, I want to record known nicknames against a Game Term, so that the editor preview can warn Editors who use them.\n63. As an Admin, I want each Hero to have a URL slug derived from its English Official name, so that Hero pages have clean addresses.\n64. As an Admin, I want to add a new Patch, which becomes the Current Patch, so that a balance patch takes one action on my side.\n65. As a Reader, I want the Current Patch shown in the site header, so that I can compare it with each Guide's Patch myself.\n66. As a Reader, I want no automatic \"outdated\" labels, so that a Guide written for 6.6 that is still valid isn't wrongly flagged.\n\n### Pages and Tournaments\n\n67. As an Admin, I want to write an About (关于) Page with a Chinese and an optional English version, so that Readers know who runs the site and how to contact us.\n68. As an Admin, I want Published Pages to appear in the public navigation automatically, so that I don't have to edit menus by hand.\n69. As an Admin, I want to post a Tournament announcement with the Tournament's date, Patch and optional cover, so that Readers learn about an upcoming in-game Tournament.\n70. As an Admin, I want to post a Tournament recap as its own item, optionally linked to its announcement, so that past Tournaments stay on record.\n71. As a Reader, I want the 锦标赛 section to list announcements and recaps newest first, each badged 预告 or 回顾, so that I can tell at a glance what each item is.\n\n### User management\n\n72. As an Admin, I want a Users page listing every account's Display name, role, state, Guide counts and last login, so that I can see who's active.\n73. As an Admin, I want to create an Editor or Admin account with an email and temporary password, so that I can invite a writer.\n74. As an Admin, I want to change a user's role, so that I can promote a trusted Editor.\n75. As an Admin, I want to apply a Submission ban (禁止投稿) to an Editor, so that they can't Submit while their Published Guides stay up.\n76. As a banned Editor, I want to see why I can't Submit, so that I'm not confused by a missing button.\n77. As an Admin, I want to deactivate and reactivate accounts, so that someone who leaves can't log in but their Published Guides stay on the site.\n78. As an Admin, I want to reset a user's password to a new temporary one, so that a writer who forgot theirs can get back in.\n79. As an Admin, I want the console to stop me from deactivating or demoting myself, and from removing the last active Admin, so that the site can't be locked out.\n80. As an Editor, I want every user-management page to refuse me, even if I type its address, so that the role split is real and not just hidden buttons.\n\n### Dashboard and content list\n\n81. As an Admin, I want my dashboard to show 待审核, total Guides by status, and \"N 项更改尚未更新到网站\", so that I know what needs my attention.\n82. As an Editor, I want my dashboard to show my Drafts, my Submitted Guides and my Returned Guides, so that I know where my work stands.\n83. As an Admin, I want to filter the content list by status, Hero, Author, Patch and language, so that I can find any Guide quickly.\n84. As an Admin or Editor, I want a success or error message after every save, so that I'm never unsure whether something worked.\n85. As an Admin or Editor, I want a console navigation that stays on every page, so that I don't get lost the way I did in WordPress.\n86. As an Admin or Editor, I want every console label in Chinese, so that the tool feels like ours.\n\n### Site build and public site\n\n87. As an Admin, I want an 更新网站 button that runs the Site build and puts the site online, so that I never have to open a terminal.\n88. As an Admin, I want a clear message if the Site build fails, such as a failed push, so that I know the site didn't update.\n89. As a Reader, I want a home page showing the Current Patch, the newest Guides and a grid of Heroes, so that I can start browsing immediately.\n90. As a Reader, I want a page per Hero listing its Guides grouped by Patch, newest first, so that I can find a build for my Hero on this Patch.\n91. As a Reader, I want a page per Author listing all their Guides, so that I can follow writers I trust.\n92. As a Reader, I want list items to show the cover image, title, Hero, Patch, Author and date, so that I can choose a Guide without opening each one.\n93. As a Reader, I want a language switch at the top right that switches the whole site, so that I can read entirely in Chinese or entirely in English.\n94. As a Reader, I want switching language on a Guide to take me to the same Guide in the other language, or to its Hero's page with a notice if it isn't available, so that the switch never leads nowhere.\n95. As an English Reader, I want only Guides with English text listed on the English site, so that I never land on a page in a language I can't read.\n96. As a Reader, I want Hero and Author pages to exist in both languages, with a \"No English guides yet\" notice when empty, so that every link works.\n97. As a Reader, I want `[[Game Term]]` markers shown as the Official name in my language, so that Item and Skill names match what I see in game.\n98. As a Reader, I want Guide addresses that stay the same after a Revision, such as `guides/vanessa-12/`, so that links shared in Bilibili comments keep working.\n99. As a Reader, I want the site to work when served from a subfolder of GitHub Pages, so that every link and image loads.\n100. As an Admin, I want Drafts, Submitted Guides, open Revisions and the Trash never to appear on the site, so that only reviewed work is public.\n101. As a Reader, I want any script or unsafe HTML in a Guide stripped, so that a Guide can never attack my browser.\n\n### Stretch\n\n102. As an Admin, I want the console hosted somewhere Editors can reach from their own computers, behind the security gate (password from the environment, rate-limited login, HTTPS, no default accounts), so that writers across China can actually use it.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n**Modules**\n\n- **Accounts.** Users, login and logout, sessions (signed cookies via itsdangerous), argon2 hashing, CSRF tokens on every state-changing form, first-login setup (password plus Display name), and account states (active / Submission ban / Deactivated).\n  - Login is by email, matching the existing `client_as` test fixture. The Display name is separate, unique, and the only name shown publicly.\n  - Roles are bundles of capabilities. Route code checks a capability, not a role name, so a rule can change without touching routes.\n- **Guide workflow.** A deep module that owns every state change and its permission check: create, save, Submit, Publish, Return (with Review notes), Unpublish, open and Submit a Revision, delete to Trash, restore, delete for good. Its interface takes the acting user and the Guide, and either performs the change or refuses with a reason the console can show. No route changes Guide status directly.\n  - Guide states: Draft → Submitted → Published, with Return and Unpublish leading back to Draft. \"In Trash\" is separate from status, so a restored Guide comes back exactly as it was.\n  - A Revision is a pending copy of a Published Guide's editable fields (texts, Hero, Patch, images, cover), with its own Draft/Submitted state. There is at most one per Guide. Publishing it overwrites the Guide's fields and updates its timestamp. The old content isn't kept. Returning it leaves the Guide untouched.\n  - Admin edits to a Published Guide apply directly with no Revision.\n  - Submit requires Chinese text and is refused under a Submission ban.\n  - Review notes belong to the Guide and each stores a quoted passage, the advice, the Admin, and the time. They are kept across rounds.\n- **Content.**\n  - Guides have per-language title and body (Chinese required to Submit, English optional), a Hero, a Patch, the Author, a cover image, and created/updated/published timestamps.\n  - Pages have per-language text, a status (Draft/Published) and an Admin-set ASCII slug. Only Admins can manage them, with no review.\n  - Tournament items are of kind announcement or recap, with per-language text, a Tournament date, a Patch, an optional cover, an optional link from recap to announcement, and a Draft/Published status. Only Admins can manage them.\n- **Game Terms and Patches.**\n  - **Game Terms:** each has one of the seven kinds, both Official names (both required), and an optional list of nicknames. Heroes also have a URL slug from the English name.\n  - **CSV import:** uses Python's standard library, previews the changes, and rejects rows per row with a reason.\n  - **Patches:** a Patch is an ordered list entry, and the newest one is the Current Patch. The Guide form offers the Current Patch and the two before it, and still shows a Guide's existing older Patch.\n- **Markdown rendering.** One function used by both the editor preview and the Site build:\n  1. Markdown is turned into HTML with markdown-it-py.\n  2. `[[term]]` markers become the Official name in the target language, matched by either language's name, and styled as a term.\n  3. The HTML is sanitized with nh3.\n\n  The same pass returns warnings (unknown terms, unmarked nicknames) for the preview. Warnings never block Submit. Review notes' quoted passages are highlighted in the preview only, never on the public site.\n- **Media.**\n  - **Accepted files:** PNG, JPG, WebP and GIF only (no SVG), checked by content as well as extension. 5 MB maximum each.\n  - **Storage:** server-generated filenames. Images are owned by a Guide (or a Tournament item) and usable from either language's text. Each image has optional per-language alt text.\n  - **Site build and deletion:** images are copied into the site output during the Site build, and deleted with their owner when it is deleted for good.\n- **Site build.** It is an extension of the existing `render_site(out)`.\n  - **Output:** two trees, `zh/` and `en/`. The root `index.html` sends Readers to `zh/`.\n  - **Pages written per language:** the home page, a Guides index, one page per Hero, one per Author with at least one Published Guide, one per Guide, the Tournaments list and each item, and each Published Page.\n  - **Language filter:** the English tree includes only items with English text. Hero and Author pages exist in both trees, with an empty notice when needed.\n  - **Links:** every link is relative, computed from each page's depth. The language switch links to the same page in the other tree, or falls back to the Hero page with a notice.\n  - **What is excluded:** only Published, non-Trash content is read, so open Revisions are never seen.\n  - **Deploy:** the existing `cms deploy` (ghp-import) puts the site online. The console's 更新网站 button runs render plus deploy and shows the result. The CLI commands stay as they are.\n  - The dashboard's \"changes not yet on the site\" count compares content change times with the last successful Site build.\n- **URLs.**\n  - **Guides:** `guides/<hero-slug>-<id>/`. The slug is generated on creation, Admins can edit it, and it is unique. It never changes on its own with a title or Revision.\n  - **Other pages:** Heroes `heroes/<slug>/`, Authors `authors/<id>/` (never the email), Tournament items `tournaments/<id>/`, Pages `<page-slug>/`.\n- **Admin console.** Server-rendered Jinja templates with Chinese labels throughout:\n  - a role-aware dashboard,\n  - the filterable content list,\n  - the Guide editor with preview, image upload, cover choice and alt text,\n  - a review screen with a Review note builder,\n  - the Users page, the Trash, Game Terms with CSV import, and Patches.\n\n  Navigation stays on every page, and every save shows a success or error message.\n- **Storage.** SQLite at `CMS_DATABASE`. The schema is created on startup. `scripts/seed_demo.py` creates one Admin and one Editor from environment passwords, plus demo Heroes, Patches, Game Terms, Guides in every status, a Page and Tournament items.\n- **Architecture.** ADR-001 and ADR-002 stand for all core work. The hosted console is a stretch ticket. When it starts, ADR-003 will supersede ADR-001 for the console, and the `CLAUDE.md` \"never on the public internet\" rule will be updated in the same change. Until then the console runs on one machine. That is a known gap for a real multi-author deployment.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **A good test** drives the system the way a user does and checks what a user would see: an HTTP response, a redirect, a page's text, or a file in the built site. Tests never inspect database rows or call private helpers, so the internals can be rebuilt without rewriting tests. Test names use the `CONTEXT.md` vocabulary (e.g. `test_editor_cannot_publish_a_submitted_guide`).\n- **Seam 1: the admin console over HTTP.** This uses the existing `client` and `client_as(role)` fixtures. It covers login and logout, account states, CSRF rejection, every permission rule (including Editors refused on Admin routes by URL), the full Guide workflow, Revisions, Review notes, Trash, Submission bans, user management guards, Game Term CSV import, Patch handling, image upload validation, and preview warnings.\n- **Seam 2: the Site build.** This uses the existing `render_site(out)` into a temporary folder, after content is set up through Seam 1. It covers:\n  - Published-only output: no Drafts, Submitted Guides, open Revisions or Trash.\n  - Relative paths only, across every generated page.\n  - Sanitized Markdown: injected script is stripped.\n  - `[[term]]` rendering per language.\n  - The English tree excluding Chinese-only items.\n  - Hero pages grouped by Patch.\n  - Author pages using Display names only.\n  - Navigation built from Published Pages.\n  - Images copied, with alt text.\n- **Isolation.** Each test gets a fresh SQLite database through `CMS_DATABASE` in a temporary folder, seeded with the `DEMO_USERS` from the test fixtures.\n- **Prior art:** `tests/test_t00.py` (HTTP and `render_site` checks, the relative-path assertion) and `tests/conftest.py` (`client_as`). The T00 tests must keep passing.\n- **Deploy** (the git push) isn't tested automatically. The button's handling of success and failure is tested with the push step replaced.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Comments and discussion. These stay on Bilibili.\n- Reader accounts.\n- Site search. Browsing by Hero, Author and Patch covers the need on a static site.\n- Translation inside the CMS (machine or AI). Writers bring their own English text.\n- A card database or patch-notes section. The community wiki already covers it.\n- Automatic \"outdated\" labels on Guides.\n- Revision history and rollback. An approved Revision replaces the old content.\n- Scheduled publishing.\n- Streamer announcements as a content type.\n- Multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, and WYSIWYG editors (excluded by the manual).\n- Hosting the console in core. It is the last stretch ticket only.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Stretch tickets planned:** (1) image uploads with alt text, which the client needs and the rubric counts as \"Media uploads with alt text\"; (2) the hosted admin console behind the security gate, done last, with ADR-003.\n- **Known gap until the hosted console exists:** Editors on their own computers can't reach a console running on one Admin's machine. In the meantime every feature is built as if the console were shared: real logins, roles, CSRF, and no default accounts.\n- Because of ADR-001, Publishing doesn't change the public site by itself. The console says so wherever it matters (\"will appear after 更新网站\").\n- Client sources: `notes/client-brief.md`, `notes/cms-field-notes.md`, `notes/research-cms-vocabulary.md`, and the grill session recorded in `CONTEXT.md`.\n\n# Handoff: 大巴扎攻略站 CMS, after #25\n\nRepo: `/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2` (a git worktree on branch\n`Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2`, reused for every ticket; do not delete it, or the branch, after merging).\nThe main checkout is `/Users/yining/code/iphs400-mp2-cms` (on `main`), which holds the real local `cms.db`.\n\n## Where things stand\n\n- **#25 (Beijing time, scrolling tables) is done, merged and closed.**\n  - PR: https://github.com/Avulpix0412/iphs400-mp2-cms/pull/28 (merge commit `3b2f3a0`; work commit `6021123`).\n    The PR body has the file map, test evidence and merge danger.\n  - The `/code-review` findings, how each was resolved, the user's choices and the decisions made while building\n    are in https://github.com/Avulpix0412/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/25#issuecomment-6245386069\n  - At handoff, 439 tests passed and pyright reported 0 errors.\n- **The branch is one commit ahead of `main`:** `c799dfb` (transcripts 15–17, handoffs 03–05, ledger rows). It\n  is pushed, and reaches `main` with the next PR.\n- **Not committed yet:** this file, this session's transcript (18, written by the SessionEnd hook), and this\n  session's ledger rows. They go into the next \"Add transcript NN\" commit, after the credential scan.\n- `.claude/state/phase` says `25`. Update it when the next stage starts.\n- **The real `cms.db` still hasn't been re-seeded since T08** (see handoff 05). Ask the user before running\n  `scripts/seed_demo.py` in the main checkout.\n\n## Next tickets (open issues; ask the user which one to take)\n\n- #11 S1 images (stretch). The spec lets a Tournament item own images and have an optional cover. T08 left\n  covers out on purpose, for this ticket.\n- #12 S2 hosted console (stretch, last; ADR-003 supersedes ADR-001 then).\n\nRead the ticket, spec #1 (`gh issue view 1`), and `CONTEXT.md` before coding, as `CLAUDE.md` requires.\n\n## What the next tickets must fit around (from #25, not obvious from the spec)\n\n- **Times are shown only through `app/times.py`.**\n  - `beijing_time` (`2026-10-17 21:05`) and `beijing_date` (`2026-10-18`) are Jinja filters in both the console\n    environment (`app/web.py`) and the site environment (`app/publish.py`).\n  - Both return `\"\"` for a NULL time.\n  - Storage and every comparison stay UTC. The offset is a fixed UTC+8, not `zoneinfo` (see the #25 comment\n    for why).\n- **`test_no_template_prints_a_stored_time_without_converting_it` scans every template.**\n  - It fails on any `{{ … }}` that names a `…_at` field without `|beijing_time` or `|beijing_date`.\n  - Name every new timestamp column `…_at` (an image's `created_at`, say), so the scan covers it.\n  - `tournament_date` is a calendar date the Admin types. {"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"0a12d330-56e0-42d6-ba9c-95ac300ed884","hash":"2b2c137476553e76ceacddc162b3ced751ab35ef57a8a2be72c4acf0ece13edb","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_013mRF5YagPD92GcxCvciD5L","type":"tool_result","content":"[project]\nname = \"iphs400-mp2-cms\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\ndescription = \"IPHS 400 MP2 — a small web CMS with a local admin console and a static public site\"\nrequires-python = \">=3.12\"\ndependencies = [\n    \"fastapi>=0.115\",\n    \"uvicorn[standard]>=0.32\",\n    \"jinja2>=3.1\",\n    \"python-multipart>=0.0.12\",   # form posts\n    \"itsdangerous>=2.2\",          # signed session cookies\n    \"argon2-cffi>=23.1\",          # password hashing (never store plain passwords)\n    \"markdown-it-py>=3.0\",        # Markdown -> HTML\n    \"nh3>=0.2\",                   # HTML sanitizer (strips <script> etc.)\n    \"ghp-import>=2.1\",            # push site/ to the gh-pages branch\n]\n\n[dependency-groups]\ndev = [\"pytest>=8.3\", \"httpx>=0.28\"]\n\n[project.scripts]\ncms = \"app.cli:main\"\n\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\ntestpaths = [\"tests\"]\n\n[build-system]\nrequires = [\"hatchling\"]\nbuild-backend = \"hatchling.build\"\n\n[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]\npackages = [\"app\"]\n\"\"\"SQLite storage. The database lives at CMS_DATABASE and is never committed.\n\nThe schema is created on connect (every statement is IF NOT EXISTS), so a fresh\nclone and a fresh test database need no separate setup step. A database made\nbefore a table gained a column gets the column added on connect (see\nADDED_COLUMNS); a schema change that adding columns can't express needs a new\ntable instead.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\n\nfrom app import settings\n\n# The time now, to the millisecond, for timestamps compared with the last Site\n# build: a Guide Published in the same second as a Site build still counts.\nNOW = \"strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%f', 'now')\"\n\nSCHEMA = f\"\"\"\n-- last_login_at was added in T09 (see ADDED_COLUMNS).\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (\n    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    email         TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE,\n    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,\n    role          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\n    display_name  TEXT UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE,\n    state         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'\n                  CHECK (state IN ('active', 'submission_ban', 'deactivated')),\n    needs_setup   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n    created_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,\n    last_login_at TEXT\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (\n    id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n    user_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\n);\n\n-- A Game Term's slug is set only for Heroes (NULLs never clash in UNIQUE).\n-- nicknames, one per line, were added in T07 (see ADDED_COLUMNS).\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS game_terms (\n    id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    kind    TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('hero', 'item', 'skill', 'enchantment',\n                                          'monster', 'merchant', 'event')),\n    name_zh TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (name_zh != ''),\n    name_en TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (name_en != ''),\n    slug    TEXT,\n    UNIQUE (kind, slug)\n);\n\n-- The Current Patch is the one added most recently (the highest id).\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS patches (\n    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    name       TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (name != ''),\n    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\n);\n\n-- A Guide's slug is filled in right after its row is created, since it ends\n-- with the Guide's own id. Status changes only through app/guides.py.\n-- A Guide is in the Trash while trashed_at is set (added in T06, as is\n-- restored_at; see ADDED_COLUMNS). That is separate from its status, so a\n-- restored Guide comes back exactly as it was; restored_at is when it last\n-- came back.\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS guides (\n    id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    slug         TEXT UNIQUE,\n    title_zh     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    body_zh      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    title_en     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    body_en      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    hero_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES game_terms (id),\n    patch_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES patches (id),\n    author_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users (id),\n    status       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft'\n                 CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'submitted', 'published')),\n    created_at   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ({NOW}),\n    updated_at   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ({NOW}),\n    published_at TEXT\n);\n\n-- A Revision is a pending change to a Published Guide, at most one per Guide.\n-- Publishing it copies it over the Guide and deletes it. base_updated_at is\n-- the Guide's updated_at when the Revision was opened, to tell whether the\n-- Guide changed since. Ids are never reused (AUTOINCREMENT), since review\n-- rounds keep the id of the Revision they Returned after it is gone.\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS revisions (\n    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    guide_id   INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES guides (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    base_updated_at TEXT NOT NULL,\n    title_zh   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    body_zh    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    title_en   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    body_en    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    hero_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES game_terms (id),\n    patch_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES patches (id),\n    status     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'submitted')),\n    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ({NOW}),\n    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ({NOW})\n);\n\n-- Each Return or Unpublish is a review round, kept for the Guide's history.\n-- A Draft with a Return or Unpublish behind it came back to its Author: a\n-- Guide only leaves Submitted or Published for Draft through one.\n-- A Return of a Revision records the Revision's id (revision_id; added in T06,\n-- see ADDED_COLUMNS). It belongs to that Revision while it is open and joins\n-- the Guide's own history once it is gone.\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS review_rounds (\n    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    guide_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES guides (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    admin_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users (id),\n    kind       TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('return', 'unpublish')),\n    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ({NOW})\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS review_notes (\n    id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    round_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES review_rounds (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    quote    TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (quote != ''),\n    advice   TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (advice != '')\n);\n\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS review_rounds_by_guide ON review_rounds (guide_id);\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS review_notes_by_round ON review_notes (round_id);\n\n-- One row per successful Site build, at the time it started reading content.\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS site_builds (\n    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    started_at TEXT NOT NULL\n);\n\n-- Pages and Tournament items are written by Admins with no review, so they are\n-- only ever Draft or Published, and only app/content.py changes them.\n-- site_changed_at is when the item last changed in a way the site shows (it\n-- was Published, edited while Published, or Unpublished), for the dashboard's\n-- count of changes not on the site.\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pages (\n    id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    slug            TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    title_zh        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    body_zh         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    title_en        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    body_en         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    status          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft'\n                    CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'published')),\n    created_at      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ({NOW}),\n    updated_at      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ({NOW}),\n    site_changed_at TEXT\n);\n\n-- A Tournament item is an announcement or a recap; a recap may link to the\n-- announcement it follows (announcement_id), and loses the link if that is\n-- deleted. tournament_date is YYYY-MM-DD. Ids are never reused\n-- (AUTOINCREMENT), since an item's address on the site is its id.\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tournament_items (\n    id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    kind            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('announcement', 'recap')),\n    title_zh        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    body_zh         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    title_en        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    body_en         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    tournament_date TEXT NOT NULL,\n    patch_id        INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES patches (id),\n    announcement_id INTEGER REFERENCES tournament_items (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,\n    status          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft'\n                    CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'published')),\n    created_at      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ({NOW}),\n    updated_at      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ({NOW}),\n    site_changed_at TEXT\n);\n\n-- Pages and Tournament items deleted for good after they were ever Published\n-- (kind is 'page' or 'tournament_item'), with their status and\n-- site_changed_at then, so the dashboard can tell whether the site still has\n-- them.\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS removed_content (\n    kind            TEXT NOT NULL,\n    item_id         INTEGER NOT NULL,\n    was_published   INTEGER NOT NULL,\n    site_changed_at TEXT NOT NULL,\n    removed_at      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ({NOW})\n);\n\n-- Published Guides deleted for good from the Trash. Their rows are gone, so\n-- this is how the dashboard still counts them as a change not on the site.\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS removed_guides (\n    guide_id   INTEGER NOT NULL,\n    removed_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ({NOW})\n);\n\"\"\"\n\n# Columns added to a table after it was first created: (table, column, type).\n# CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS leaves an older table as it was, so connect()\n# adds whichever of these it lacks.\nADDED_COLUMNS = [\n    (\"users\", \"last_login_at\", \"TEXT\"),\n    (\"guides\", \"trashed_at\", \"TEXT\"),\n    (\"guides\", \"restored_at\", \"TEXT\"),\n    (\"review_rounds\", \"revision_id\", \"INTEGER\"),\n    (\"game_terms\", \"nicknames\", \"TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''\"),\n]\n\n# Indexes on added columns, made once the columns are sure to exist.\nINDEXES = \"\"\"\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS review_rounds_by_revision ON review_rounds (revision_id);\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _add_missing_columns(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:\n    for table, column, type_ in ADDED_COLUMNS:\n        existing = {row[\"name\"] for row in conn.execute(f\"PRAGMA table_info({table})\")}\n        if column not in existing:\n            conn.execute(f\"ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN {column} {type_}\")\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef connect() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\n    \"\"\"Open the database, commit if the block succeeds, and always close.\"\"\"\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(settings.database_path())\n    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    conn.execute(\"PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON\")\n    try:\n        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n hard-code secrets).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nTEMPLATES = ROOT / \"templates\"\nSITE = ROOT / e.g.\n# https://yourname.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\nBASE_PATH = os.environ.get(\"CMS_BASE_PATH\", \"\")\n\n\ndef database_path() -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Read on every connect, so tests can point Publishing the Revision copies it over the\n12\tGuide; Returning it leaves the Guide alone.
