{"parentUuid":"4f2160c1-fd81-4ec3-8c13-0f18ad57db23","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"file","filename":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/app/media.py","content":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/app/media.py","content":"\"\"\"Uploaded images: checking them, storing them, and the rows that say whose\nthey are.\n\nAn image belongs to one owner, a Guide, a Guide's open Revision or a\nTournament item, named by a key such as \"guide/12\" (its `media_owner`). It can be\nused in both languages' text, as `![](<filename>)`, and has optional alt text\nper language. The owner's cover is one of its images, by file name, kept on\nthe owner's own row: NULL means the first image, and '' means none.\n\nOnly PNG, JPG, WebP and GIF are accepted, recognised by their content (an SVG\ncan carry script, so it never is). The stored file name is generated here;\nthe uploaded name is only checked for its extension and never touches the\ndisk. Files live in the media folder (settings.media_path()), the store of\nImages' files. A Revision's images are copies of its Guide's rows that share\ntheir files, so a file is deleted only once no row names it. Files are\nwritten and deleted along with the transaction that adds or removes their\nrows (db.after_commit).\n\nWho may change an owner's images is decided by app/guides.py and\napp/content.py, which call these functions once they have checked.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport secrets\nimport shutil\nimport sqlite3\nfrom collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom app import db, settings\n\nMAX_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024\nALLOWED = \"PNG、JPG、WebP 或 GIF\"\nEXTENSIONS = {\".png\", \".jpg\", \".jpeg\", \".webp\", \".gif\"}\nCONTENT_TYPES = {\".png\": \"image/png\", \".jpg\": \"image/jpeg\", \".webp\": \"image/webp\",\n                 \".gif\": \"image/gif\"}\nFILENAME = re.compile(r\"[0-9a-f]{32}\\.(png|jpg|webp|gif)\")\n\n\nclass BadImage(Exception):\n    \"\"\"An upload that is refused, with the reason to show.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, message: str) -> None:\n        super().__init__(message)\n        self.message = message\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Upload:\n    \"\"\"A file as the browser sent it. `data` holds at most MAX_BYTES + 1\n    bytes, enough to tell that a file is too large.\"\"\"\n    name: str\n    data: bytes\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Image:\n    id: int\n    filename: str\n    alt_zh: str\n    alt_en: str\n\n    def alt(self, lang: str) -> str:\n        return getattr(self, f\"alt_{lang}\")\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ImageFields:\n    \"\"\"What an editor form sends about its images: alt text by image id, as\n    (Chinese, English), for the images it showed, and the chosen cover's file\n    name. cover is None when the form sent no choice.\"\"\"\n    alts: Mapping[int, tuple[str, str]] = field(default_factory=dict)\n    cover: str | None = None\n\n\ndef _kind_by_content(data: bytes) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The extension that `data` really is, by its first bytes.\"\"\"\n    if data.startswith(b\"\\x89PNG\\r\\n\\x1a\\n\"):\n        return \".png\"\n    if data.startswith(b\"\\xff\\xd8\\xff\"):\n        return \".jpg\"\n    if data[:4] == b\"RIFF\" and data[8:12] == b\"WEBP\":\n        return \".webp\"\n    if data[:6] in (b\"GIF87a\", b\"GIF89a\"):\n        return \".gif\"\n    return None\n\n\ndef checked(upload: Upload) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The extension to store `upload` under, or BadImage saying why not.\"\"\"\n    if not upload.name and not upload.data:\n        raise BadImage(\"请先选择要上传的图片。\")\n    extension = Path(upload.name.lower()).suffix\n    if extension not in EXTENSIONS:\n        raise BadImage(f\"只能上传 {ALLOWED} 图片（不支持 SVG），\"\n                       f\"“{upload.name}”不是。\")\n    if len(upload.data) > MAX_BYTES:\n        raise BadImage(f\"图片不能超过 5 MB，“{upload.name}”太大了。\")\n    kind = _kind_by_content(upload.data)\n    if kind is None:\n        raise BadImage(f\"“{upload.name}”的内容不是 {ALLOWED} 图片，\"\n                       \"可能只是改了扩展名。\")\n    return kind\n\n\ndef images(conn: sqlite3.Connection, owner: str) -> list[Image]:\n    \"\"\"The owner's images, in the order they were uploaded.\"\"\"\n    rows = conn.execute(\"SELECT id, filename, alt_zh, alt_en FROM images\"\n                        \" WHERE owner = ? ORDER BY id\", (owner,)).fetchall()\n    return [Image(**dict(row)) for row in rows]\n\n\ndef add(conn: sqlite3.Connection, owner: str, upload: Upload) -> Image:\n    \"\"\"Check `upload` and store it as the owner's newest image.\"\"\"\n    filename = secrets.token_hex(16) + checked(upload)\n    folder = settings.media_path()\n    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    (folder / filename).write_bytes(upload.data)\n    db.after_commit(conn, rolled_back=(folder / filename).unlink)\n    cur = conn.execute(\"INSERT INTO images (owner, filename) VALUES (?, ?)\",\n                       (owner, filename))\n    return Image(cur.lastrowid or 0, filename, \"\", \"\")\n\n\ndef image(conn: sqlite3.Connection, owner: str, image_id: int) -> Image | None:\n    return next((found for found in images(conn, owner) if found.id == image_id), None)\n\n\ndef file(conn: sqlite3.Connection, owner: str, filename: str) -> Path | None:\n    \"\"\"The file of the owner's image called `filename`, if it has one.\"\"\"\n    if not FILENAME.fullmatch(filename) or not any(\n            found.filename == filename for found in images(conn, owner)):\n        return None\n    path = settings.media_path() / filename\n    return path if path.is_file() else None\n\n\ndef content_type(filename: str) -> str:\n    return CONTENT_TYPES[Path(filename).suffix]\n\n\ndef save_alts(conn: sqlite3.Connection, owner: str, fields: ImageFields) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Keep the alt text the form sent for the owner's images.\"\"\"\n    conn.executemany(\"UPDATE images SET alt_zh = ?, alt_en = ? WHERE id = ? AND owner = ?\",\n                     [(zh.strip(), en.strip(), image_id, owner)\n                      for image_id, (zh, en) in fields.alts.items()])\n\n\ndef checked_cover(conn: sqlite3.Connection, owner: str, cover: str | None, *,\n                  optional: bool) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The cover to keep from what a form sent: None (the first image) unless\n    it names one of the owner's images, or is '' and the owner may have no\n    cover at all.\"\"\"\n    if cover == \"\" and optional:\n        return \"\"\n    return cover if any(found.filename == cover for found in images(conn, owner)) else None\n\n\ndef cover(found: list[Image], chosen: str | None) -> Image | None:\n    \"\"\"The cover among `found` (an owner's images): the chosen one, else the\n    first, or none if the owner chose none or has no images.\"\"\"\n    if chosen == \"\":\n        return None\n    return next((image for image in found if image.filename == chosen),\n                found[0] if found else None)\n\n\ndef _delete_unused_files(conn: sqlite3.Connection, filenames: Iterable[str]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Delete the files no image row names any more, once that is committed.\"\"\"\n    for filename in set(filenames):\n        if not conn.execute(\"SELECT 1 FROM images WHERE filename = ?\",\n                            (filename,)).fetchone():\n            db.after_commit(conn, committed=lambda path=settings.media_path() / filename:\n                            path.unlink(missing_ok=True))\n\n\ndef remove_unused(conn: sqlite3.Connection, owner: str, image_id: int,\n                  body_zh: str, body_en: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Delete the owner's image, unless its text (`body_zh`, `body_en`) still\n    uses it, which raises BadImage. False if the owner has no such image.\"\"\"\n    found = image(conn, owner, image_id)\n    if found is None:\n        return False\n    # Written `![alt](<filename>)`, with any spaces or angle brackets\n    # Markdown allows around the address.\n    used = re.compile(rf\"!\\[[^\\]]*\\]\\(\\s*<?{re.escape(found.filename)}[\\s>)]\")\n    for where, body in [(\"中文正文\", body_zh), (\"英文正文\", body_en)]:\n        if used.search(body):\n            raise BadImage(f\"{where}还在使用这张图片。请先从{where}里删掉\"\n                           f\" ![]({found.filename})，再删除图片。\")\n    conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM images WHERE id = ?\", (image_id,))\n    _delete_unused_files(conn, [found.filename])\n    return True\n\n\ndef remove_all(conn: sqlite3.Connection, owner: str) -> None:\n    filenames = [found.filename for found in images(conn, owner)]\n    conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM images WHERE owner = ?\", (owner,))\n    _delete_unused_files(conn, filenames)\n\n\ndef copy_all(conn: sqlite3.Connection, source: str, target: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Give `target` its own copy of each of `source`'s images (rows only;\n    the two share the files).\"\"\"\n    remove_all(conn, target)\n    conn.execute(\"INSERT INTO images (owner, filename, alt_zh, alt_en)\"\n                 \" SELECT ?, filename, alt_zh, alt_en FROM images WHERE owner = ?\"\n                 \" ORDER BY id\", (target, source))\n\n\ndef move_all(conn: sqlite3.Connection, source: str, target: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Replace `target`'s images with `source`'s, which `source` loses.\"\"\"\n    old = [found.filename for found in images(conn, target)]\n    conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM images WHERE owner = ?\", (target,))\n    conn.execute(\"UPDATE images SET owner = ? WHERE owner = ?\", (target, source))\n    _delete_unused_files(conn, old)\n\n\ndef sources(found: list[Image], lang: str, src: str) -> dict[str, tuple[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"What render_markdown needs to show `found` (an owner's images) on one\n    page in `lang`: each file name, as written in the text, mapped to the\n    `src` to use there (`src` with \"{}\" in place of the file name) and its alt\n    text in `lang`.\"\"\"\n    return {image.filename: (src.format(image.filename), image.alt(lang))\n            for image in found}\n\n\ndef copy_files(found: Iterable[Image], out: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Copy the files of the images `found` into the folder `out`.\"\"\"\n    for image in found:\n        source = settings.media_path() / image.filename\n        if source.is_file():\n            out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n            shutil.copyfile(source, out / image.filename)\n","numLines":237,"startLine":1,"totalLines":237}},"displayPath":"app/media.py"},"type":"attachment","uuid":"e8cb7aee-ad4e-44be-a605-20b898601e0b","timestamp":"2026-10-18T05:54:41.603Z","rendered":[{"content":"<system-reminder>\nCalled the Read tool with the following input: {\"file_path\":\"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/app/media.py\"}\n</system-reminder>"},{"content":"<system-reminder>\nResult of calling the Read tool:\n1\t\"\"\"Uploaded images: checking them, storing them, and the rows that say whose\n2\tthey are.\n3\t\n4\tAn image belongs to one owner, a Guide, a Guide's open Revision or a\n5\tTournament item, named by a key such as \"guide/12\" (its `media_owner`). The user decides.\n\n## Completion Status Protocol\n\nWhen completing a skill workflow, report status using one of:\n- **DONE** — completed with evidence.\n- **DONE_WITH_CONCERNS** — completed, but list concerns.\n- **BLOCKED** — cannot proceed; state blocker and what was tried.\n- **NEEDS_CONTEXT** — missing info; state exactly what is needed.\n\nEscalate after 3 failed attempts, uncertain security-sensitive changes, or scope you cannot verify. Format: `STATUS`, `REASON`, `ATTEMPTED`, `RECOMMENDATION`.\n\n## Operational Self-Improvement\n\nBefore completing, if you discovered a durable project quirk or command fix that would save 5+ minutes next time, log it:\n\n```bash\n~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-learnings-log '{\"skill\":\"SKILL_NAME\",\"type\":\"operational\",\"key\":\"SHORT_KEY\",\"insight\":\"DESCRIPTION\",\"confidence\":N,\"source\":\"observed\"}'\n```\n\nDo not log obvious facts or one-time transient errors.\n\n## Telemetry (run last)\n\nAfter workflow completion, log telemetry. Use skill `name:` from frontmatter. OUTCOME is success/error/abort/unknown.\n\n**PLAN MODE EXCEPTION — ALWAYS RUN:** This command writes telemetry to\n`~/.gstack/analytics/`, matching preamble analytics writes.\n\nRun this bash:\n\n```bash\n_TEL_END=$(date +%s)\n_TEL_DUR=$(( _TEL_END - _TEL_START ))\nrm -f ~/.gstack/analytics/.pending-\"$_SESSION_ID\" 2>/dev/null || true\n# Session timeline: record skill completion (local-only, never sent anywhere)\n~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-timeline-log '{\"skill\":\"SKILL_NAME\",\"event\":\"completed\",\"branch\":\"'$(git branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)'\",\"outcome\":\"OUTCOME\",\"duration_s\":\"'\"$_TEL_DUR\"'\",\"session\":\"'\"$_SESSION_ID\"'\"}' 2>/dev/null || true\n# Local analytics (gated on telemetry setting)\nif [ \"$_TEL\" != \"off\" ]; then\necho '{\"skill\":\"SKILL_NAME\",\"duration_s\":\"'\"$_TEL_DUR\"'\",\"outcome\":\"OUTCOME\",\"browse\":\"USED_BROWSE\",\"session\":\"'\"$_SESSION_ID\"'\",\"ts\":\"'$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)'\"}' >> ~/.gstack/analytics/skill-usage.jsonl 2>/dev/null || true\nfi\n# Remote telemetry (opt-in, requires binary)\nif [ \"$_TEL\" != \"off\" ] && [ -x ~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-telemetry-log ]; then\n  ~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-telemetry-log \\\n    --skill \"SKILL_NAME\" --duration \"$_TEL_DUR\" --outcome \"OUTCOME\" \\\n    --used-browse \"USED_BROWSE\" --session-id \"$_SESSION_ID\" 2>/dev/null &\nfi\n```\n\nReplace `SKILL_NAME`, `OUTCOME`, and `USED_BROWSE` before running.\n\n## Plan Status Footer\n\nIn plan mode before ExitPlanMode: if the plan file lacks `## GSTACK REVIEW REPORT`, run `~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-review-read` and append the standard runs/status/findings table. With `NO_REVIEWS` or empty, append a 5-row placeholder with verdict \"NO REVIEWS YET — run `/autoplan`\". If a richer report exists, skip.\n\nPLAN MODE EXCEPTION — always allowed (it's the plan file).\n\n# browse: QA Testing & Dogfooding\n\nPersistent headless Chromium. First call auto-starts (~3s), then ~100ms per command.\nState persists between calls (cookies, tabs, login sessions).\n\n## SETUP (run this check BEFORE any browse command)\n\n```bash\n_ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)\nB=\"\"\n[ -n \"$_ROOT\" ] && [ -x \"$_ROOT/.claude/skills/gstack/browse/dist/browse\" ] && B=\"$_ROOT/.claude/skills/gstack/browse/dist/browse\"\n[ -z \"$B\" ] && B=\"$HOME/.claude/skills/gstack/browse/dist/browse\"\nif [ -x \"$B\" ]; then\n  echo \"READY: $B\"\nelse\n  echo \"NEEDS_SETUP\"\nfi\n```\n\nIf `NEEDS_SETUP`:\n1. Tell the user: \"gstack browse needs a one-time build (~10 seconds). OK to proceed?\" Then STOP and wait.\n2. Run: `cd <SKILL_DIR> && ./setup`\n3. If `bun` is not installed:\n   ```bash\n   if ! command -v bun >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n     BUN_VERSION=\"1.3.10\"\n     BUN_INSTALL_SHA=\"bab8acfb046aac8c72407bdcce903957665d655d7acaa3e11c7c4616beae68dd\"\n     tmpfile=$(mktemp)\n     curl -fsSL \"https://bun.sh/install\" -o \"$tmpfile\"\n     actual_sha=$(shasum -a 256 \"$tmpfile\" | awk '{print $1}')\n     if [ \"$actual_sha\" != \"$BUN_INSTALL_SHA\" ]; then\n       echo \"ERROR: bun install script checksum mismatch\" >&2\n\n[... skill content truncated for compaction; use Read on the skill path if you need the full text]"},{"name":"mattpocock-skills:tdd","path":"plugin:mattpocock-skills:tdd","content":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/yining/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.3.1/skills/engineering/tdd\n\n# Test-Driven Development\n\nTDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\n\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `GLOSSARY.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\n## What a good test is\n\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: \"user can checkout with valid cart\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.\n\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\n\n## Seams: where tests go\n\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\n\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\n\nAsk: \"What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?\" Give each proposed seam a one-line note on what it catches and what it misses.\n\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \"codebase-design\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\n\n## Anti-patterns\n\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\n\n## Rules of the loop\n\n- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.\n- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.\n- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.\n"},{"name":"mattpocock-skills:implement","path":"plugin:mattpocock-skills:implement","content":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/yining/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.3.1/skills/engineering/implement\n\nImplement the work described by the user in the spec or tickets.\n\nIf the user passes a ticket reference, fetch it from the issue tracker and state its title before starting. If the reference is ambiguous, ask.\n\nCall the Skill tool with \"tdd\" where possible, at pre-agreed seams.\n\nRun typechecking regularly, single test files regularly, and the full test suite once at the end.\n\nOnce done, call the Skill tool with \"code-review\" to review the work.\n\nCommit your work to the current branch.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: #11"}]},"type":"attachment","uuid":"288b2b0e-c10a-456e-a0de-4faad5d4aa48","timestamp":"2026-10-18T05:54:41.604Z","rendered":[{"content":"<system-reminder>\nThe following skills were invoked EARLIER in this session (before the conversation was compacted), not on the current turn. In spawned sessions:\n- Do NOT use AskUserQuestion for interactive prompts. Auto-choose the recommended option.\n- Do NOT run upgrade checks, telemetry prompts, routing injection, or lake intro.\n- Focus on completing the task and reporting results via prose output.\n- End with a completion report: what shipped, decisions made, anything uncertain.\n\n## GBrain Sync (skill start)\n\n```bash\n_GSTACK_HOME=\"${GSTACK_HOME:-$HOME/.gstack}\"\n_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE=\"$HOME/.gstack-brain-remote.txt\"\n_BRAIN_SYNC_BIN=\"~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-brain-sync\"\n_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN=\"~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-config\"\n\n_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE=$(\"$_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN\" get gbrain_sync_mode 2>/dev/null || echo off)\n\nif [ -f \"$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE\" ] && [ ! -d \"$_GSTACK_HOME/.git\" ] && [ \"$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE\" = \"off\" ]; then\n  _BRAIN_NEW_URL=$(head -1 \"$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE\" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')\n  if [ -n \"$_BRAIN_NEW_URL\" ]; then\n    echo \"BRAIN_SYNC: brain repo detected: $_BRAIN_NEW_URL\"\n    echo \"BRAIN_SYNC: run 'gstack-brain-restore' to pull your cross-machine memory (or 'gstack-config set gbrain_sync_mode off' to dismiss forever)\"\n  fi\nfi\n\nif [ -d \"$_GSTACK_HOME/.git\" ] && [ \"$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE\" != \"off\" ]; then\n  _BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE=\"$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-last-pull\"\n  _BRAIN_NOW=$(date +%s)\n  _BRAIN_DO_PULL=1\n  if [ -f \"$_BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE\" ]; then\n    _BRAIN_LAST=$(cat \"$_BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)\n    _BRAIN_AGE=$(( _BRAIN_NOW - _BRAIN_LAST ))\n    [ \"$_BRAIN_AGE\" -lt 86400 ] && _BRAIN_DO_PULL=0\n  fi\n  if [ \"$_BRAIN_DO_PULL\" = \"1\" ]; then\n    ( cd \"$_GSTACK_HOME\" && git fetch origin >/dev/null 2>&1 && git merge --ff-only \"origin/$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)\" >/dev/null 2>&1 ) || true\n    echo \"$_BRAIN_NOW\" > \"$_BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE\"\n  fi\n  \"$_BRAIN_SYNC_BIN\" --once 2>/dev/null || true\nfi\n\nif [ -d \"$_GSTACK_HOME/.git\" ] && [ \"$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE\" != \"off\" ]; then\n  _BRAIN_QUEUE_DEPTH=0\n  [ -f \"$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-queue.jsonl\" ] && _BRAIN_QUEUE_DEPTH=$(wc -l < \"$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-queue.jsonl\" | tr -d ' ')\n  _BRAIN_LAST_PUSH=\"never\"\n  [ -f \"$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-last-push\" ] && _BRAIN_LAST_PUSH=$(cat \"$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-last-push\" 2>/dev/null || echo never)\n  echo \"BRAIN_SYNC: mode=$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE | last_push=$_BRAIN_LAST_PUSH | queue=$_BRAIN_QUEUE_DEPTH\"\nelse\n  echo \"BRAIN_SYNC: off\"\nfi\n```\n\n\n\nPrivacy stop-gate: if output shows `BRAIN_SYNC: off`, `gbrain_sync_mode_prompted` is `false`, and gbrain is on PATH or `gbrain doctor --fast --json` works, ask once:\n\n> gstack can publish your session memory to a private GitHub repo that GBrain indexes across machines. How much should sync?\n\nOptions:\n- A) Everything allowlisted (recommended)\n- B) Only artifacts\n- C) Decline, keep everything local\n\nAfter answer:\n\n```bash\n# Chosen mode: full | artifacts-only | off\n\"$_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN\" set gbrain_sync_mode <choice>\n\"$_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN\" set gbrain_sync_mode_prompted true\n```\n\nIf A/B and `~/.gstack/.git` is missing, ask whether to run `gstack-brain-init`. Do not block the skill.\n\nAt skill END before telemetry:\n\n```bash\n\"~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-brain-sync\" --discover-new 2>/dev/null || true\n\"~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-brain-sync\" --once 2>/dev/null || true\n```\n\n\n## Model-Specific Behavioral Patch (claude)\n\nThe following nudges are tuned for the claude model family. They are\n**subordinate** to skill workflow, STOP points, AskUserQuestion gates, plan-mode\nsafety, and /ship review gates. If a nudge below conflicts with skill instructions,\nthe skill wins. Treat these as preferences, not rules.\n\n**Todo-list discipline.** When working through a multi-step plan, mark each task\ncomplete individually as you finish it. Do not batch-complete at the end. If a task\nturns out to be unnecessary, mark it skipped with a one-line reason.\n\n**Think before heavy actions.** For complex operations (refactors, migrations,\nnon-trivial new features), briefly state your approach before executing. This lets\nthe user course-correct cheaply instead of mid-flight.\n\n**Dedicated tools over Bash.** Prefer Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep over shell\nequivalents (cat, sed, find, grep). The dedicated tools are cheaper and clearer.\n\n## Voice\n\nDirect, concrete, builder-to-builder. Name the file, function, command, and user-visible impact. No filler.\n\nNo em dashes. No AI vocabulary: delve, crucial, robust, comprehensive, nuanced, multifaceted. Never corporate or academic. Short paragraphs. End with what to do.\n\nThe user has context you do not. Cross-model agreement is a recommendation, not a decision. The user decides.\n\n## Completion Status Protocol\n\nWhen completing a skill workflow, report status using one of:\n- **DONE** — completed with evidence.\n- **DONE_WITH_CONCERNS** — completed, but list concerns.\n- **BLOCKED** — cannot proceed; state blocker and what was tried.\n- **NEEDS_CONTEXT** — missing info; state exactly what is needed.\n\nEscalate after 3 failed attempts, uncertain security-sensitive changes, or scope you cannot verify. Format: `STATUS`, `REASON`, `ATTEMPTED`, `RECOMMENDATION`.\n\n## Operational Self-Improvement\n\nBefore completing, if you discovered a durable project quirk or command fix that would save 5+ minutes next time, log it:\n\n```bash\n~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-learnings-log '{\"skill\":\"SKILL_NAME\",\"type\":\"operational\",\"key\":\"SHORT_KEY\",\"insight\":\"DESCRIPTION\",\"confidence\":N,\"source\":\"observed\"}'\n```\n\nDo not log obvious facts or one-time transient errors.\n\n## Telemetry (run last)\n\nAfter workflow completion, log telemetry. Use skill `name:` from frontmatter. OUTCOME is success/error/abort/unknown.\n\n**PLAN MODE EXCEPTION — ALWAYS RUN:** This command writes telemetry to\n`~/.gstack/analytics/`, matching preamble analytics writes.\n\nRun this bash:\n\n```bash\n_TEL_END=$(date +%s)\n_TEL_DUR=$(( _TEL_END - _TEL_START ))\nrm -f ~/.gstack/analytics/.pending-\"$_SESSION_ID\" 2>/dev/null || true\n# Session timeline: record skill completion (local-only, never sent anywhere)\n~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-timeline-log '{\"skill\":\"SKILL_NAME\",\"event\":\"completed\",\"branch\":\"'$(git branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)'\",\"outcome\":\"OUTCOME\",\"duration_s\":\"'\"$_TEL_DUR\"'\",\"session\":\"'\"$_SESSION_ID\"'\"}' 2>/dev/null || true\n# Local analytics (gated on telemetry setting)\nif [ \"$_TEL\" != \"off\" ]; then\necho '{\"skill\":\"SKILL_NAME\",\"duration_s\":\"'\"$_TEL_DUR\"'\",\"outcome\":\"OUTCOME\",\"browse\":\"USED_BROWSE\",\"session\":\"'\"$_SESSION_ID\"'\",\"ts\":\"'$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)'\"}' >> ~/.gstack/analytics/skill-usage.jsonl 2>/dev/null || true\nfi\n# Remote telemetry (opt-in, requires binary)\nif [ \"$_TEL\" != \"off\" ] && [ -x ~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-telemetry-log ]; then\n  ~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-telemetry-log \\\n    --skill \"SKILL_NAME\" --duration \"$_TEL_DUR\" --outcome \"OUTCOME\" \\\n    --used-browse \"USED_BROWSE\" --session-id \"$_SESSION_ID\" 2>/dev/null &\nfi\n```\n\nReplace `SKILL_NAME`, `OUTCOME`, and `USED_BROWSE` before running.\n\n## Plan Status Footer\n\nIn plan mode before ExitPlanMode: if the plan file lacks `## GSTACK REVIEW REPORT`, run `~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-review-read` and append the standard runs/status/findings table. With `NO_REVIEWS` or empty, append a 5-row placeholder with verdict \"NO REVIEWS YET — run `/autoplan`\". If a richer report exists, skip.\n\nPLAN MODE EXCEPTION — always allowed (it's the plan file).\n\n# browse: QA Testing & Dogfooding\n\nPersistent headless Chromium. First call auto-starts (~3s), then ~100ms per command.\nState persists between calls (cookies, tabs, login sessions).\n\n## SETUP (run this check BEFORE any browse command)\n\n```bash\n_ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)\nB=\"\"\n[ -n \"$_ROOT\" ] && [ -x \"$_ROOT/.claude/skills/gstack/browse/dist/browse\" ] && B=\"$_ROOT/.claude/skills/gstack/browse/dist/browse\"\n[ -z \"$B\" ] && B=\"$HOME/.claude/skills/gstack/browse/dist/browse\"\nif [ -x \"$B\" ]; then\n  echo \"READY: $B\"\nelse\n  echo \"NEEDS_SETUP\"\nfi\n```\n\nIf `NEEDS_SETUP`:\n1. Tell the user: \"gstack browse needs a one-time build (~10 seconds). OK to proceed?\" Then STOP and wait.\n2. Run: `cd <SKILL_DIR> && ./setup`\n3. If `bun` is not installed:\n   ```bash\n   if ! command -v bun >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n     BUN_VERSION=\"1.3.10\"\n     BUN_INSTALL_SHA=\"bab8acfb046aac8c72407bdcce903957665d655d7acaa3e11c7c4616beae68dd\"\n     tmpfile=$(mktemp)\n     curl -fsSL \"https://bun.sh/install\" -o \"$tmpfile\"\n     actual_sha=$(shasum -a 256 \"$tmpfile\" | awk '{print $1}')\n     if [ \"$actual_sha\" != \"$BUN_INSTALL_SHA\" ]; then\n       echo \"ERROR: bun install script checksum mismatch\" >&2\n\n[... skill content truncated for compaction; use Read on the skill path if you need the full text]\n\n---\n\n### Skill: mattpocock-skills:tdd\nPath: plugin:mattpocock-skills:tdd\n\nBase directory for this skill: /Users/yining/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.3.1/skills/engineering/tdd\n\n# Test-Driven Development\n\nTDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\n\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `GLOSSARY.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\n## What a good test is\n\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: \"user can checkout with valid cart\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.\n\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\n\n## Seams: where tests go\n\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\n\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\n\nAsk: \"What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?\" Give each proposed seam a one-line note on what it catches and what it misses.\n\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \"codebase-design\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\n\n## Anti-patterns\n\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\n\n## Rules of the loop\n\n- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.\n- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.\n- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.\n\n\n---\n\n### Skill: mattpocock-skills:implement\nPath: plugin:mattpocock-skills:implement\n\nBase directory for this skill: /Users/yining/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.3.1/skills/engineering/implement\n\nImplement the work described by the user in the spec or tickets.\n\nIf the user passes a ticket reference, fetch it from the issue tracker and state its title before starting. If the reference is ambiguous, ask.\n\nCall the Skill tool with \"tdd\" where possible, at pre-agreed seams.\n\nRun typechecking regularly, single test files regularly, and the full test suite once at the end.\n\nOnce done, call the Skill tool with \"code-review\" to review the work.\n\nCommit your work to the current branch.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: #11\n</system-reminder>"}],"renderedRole":"system","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"0a12d330-56e0-42d6-ba9c-95ac300ed884","version":"2.1.302","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","slug":"glowing-swimming-stearns"}

FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)\n- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions (\"Can Claude...\", \"Does Claude...\", \"How do I...\") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)\n- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: \"medium\" for moderate exploration, \"very thorough\" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)\n- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)\n- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)\n- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)\n</system-reminder>"}],"renderedRole":"system","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"0a12d330-56e0-42d6-ba9c-95ac300ed884","version":"2.1.302","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","slug":"glowing-swimming-stearns"}

Reviews and publishes other\n13\tpeople's Guides and manages users.\n14\t_Avoid_: owner, superuser\n15\t\n16\t**Editor** (编辑):\n17\tAn invited guide writer (another up主 or an experienced player). Writes\n18\tGuides but cannot publish them or manage users.\n19\t_Avoid_: author (as a role name), contributor, writer\n20\t\n21\t**Reader** (读者):\n22\tAnyone who plays the game and reads the public site. Readers can browse all of an Author's\n27\tPublished Guides on that Author's page.\n28\t_Avoid_: owner, creator, up主 (not every Author is a streamer)\n29\t\n30\t**Submission ban** (禁止投稿):\n31\tAn account state in which an Editor can still log in and work on Drafts but\n32\tcannot Submit Guides or Revisions. Their Published Guides stay on the site.\n33\t_Avoid_: suspension, block, mute\n34\t\n35\t**Deactivated** (已停用):\n36\tAn account state in which the person cannot log in at all. Their Published\n37\tGuides stay on the site.\n38\t_Avoid_: deleted, disabled, banned\n39\t\n40\t**First-login setup** (首次登录设置):\n41\tThe step a person with a temporary password must finish before using the\n42\tconsole: they choose their own password and their Display name.\n43\t_Avoid_: onboarding, activation, registration\n44\t\n45\t**Display name** (昵称):\n46\tThe name an Author chooses to be shown under publicly. It is never their\n47\tlogin username.\n48\t_Avoid_: username, handle\n49\t\n50\t### Content\n51\t\n52\t**Guide** (攻略):\n53\tA written strategy piece about one Hero on one Patch, typically built around\n54\tscreenshots of a lineup or deck with an explanation of how it plays. Guides\n55\tfor tournament mode are still Guides.\n56\t_Avoid_: article, tutorial, post\n57\t\n58\t**Page** (页面):\n59\tA standalone piece of site content written by an Admin, such as About (关于),\n60\tthat appears in the public navigation once Published, after 攻略 and 锦标赛, in\n61\tthe order Pages were added. Its address is an Admin-set ASCII Slug. Pages are\n62\tnever reviewed: a Page is a Draft or Published, and deleting one is for good\n63\t(the Trash is for Guides only).\n64\t_Avoid_: static page\n65\t\n66\t**Tournament announcement** (锦标赛预告):\n67\tAn Admin-written notice about an upcoming in-game Tournament.\n68\t_Avoid_: event, news, post\n69\t\n70\t**Tournament recap** (锦标赛回顾):\n71\tAn Admin-written account of a Tournament that has already happened. It is a\n72\tseparate item from that Tournament's announcement, which it may link to.\n73\t_Avoid_: event, report, result\n74\t\n75\t**Tournament item** (锦标赛内容):\n76\tA Tournament announcement or a Tournament recap. Each has the Tournament's\n77\tdate and Patch. Like Pages, they are never reviewed: each is a Draft or\n78\tPublished, and deleting one is for good. The 锦标赛 section lists them newest\n79\tTournament date first, badged 预告 or 回顾.\n80\t_Avoid_: event, post, news\n81\t\n82\t**Chinese text / English text** (中文版 / 英文版):\n83\tThe two language versions of a Guide (or other content), each with its own\n84\ttitle and body. Chinese is required. English is optional, and content without\n85\tit does not appear on the English site.\n86\t_Avoid_: translation, localization, body\n87\t\n88\t**Image** (图片):\n89\tA screenshot (PNG, JPG, WebP or GIF, at most 5 MB) uploaded into one Guide or\n90\tTournament item. It belongs to that item, can be used in both its Chinese\n91\ttext and its English text, and is deleted with it. A Revision has its own copy\n92\tof its Guide's images.\n93\t_Avoid_: attachment, picture, file (in code, the media folder is just where\n94\tImages' files are stored)\n95\t\n96\t**Alt text** (图片说明):\n97\tAn Image's optional short description, one per language, shown in place of\n98\tthe Image to Readers whose screen reader reads it or whose image fails to\n99\tload.\n100\t_Avoid_: caption, description, title\n101\t\n102\t**Cover** (封面):\n103\tThe Image shown with an item in the site's lists. A Guide's is its first Image\n104\tunless the writer chooses another; a Tournament item may also have none.\n105\t_Avoid_: featured image, banner\n106\t\n107\t### The game\n108\t\n109\t**Game Term** (游戏术语):\n110\tA named thing in The Bazaar that has an official Chinese name and an official\n111\tEnglish name, stored as a pair. It is one of seven kinds: Hero, Item, Skill,\n112\tEnchantment, Monster, Merchant, or Event.\n113\t_Avoid_: keyword, tag, entity\n114\t\n115\t**Item** (物品):\n116\tThe Game Term kind for the cards a player builds with.\n117\t_Avoid_: card\n118\t\n119\t**Event** (事件):\n120\tThe Game Term kind for an in-game event a player encounters during a run. The\n121\tword means only this; it is never used for a Tournament.\n122\t_Avoid_: using \"event\" for Tournaments or site activity\n123\t\n124\t**Hero** (英雄):\n125\tThe Game Term for a playable character. Every Guide is about exactly one Hero.\n126\tNo two Heroes share an English Official name (ignoring case).\n127\t_Avoid_: character, class\n128\t\n129\t**Official name** (官方名称):\n130\tThe name the game itself uses for a Game Term in a given language. The site\n131\tonly ever shows Official names.\n132\t_Avoid_: nickname (外号), alias, translation\n133\t\n134\t**Nickname** (外号):\n135\tA name players use for a Game Term that the game itself doesn't, such as 瓦姐\n136\tfor 瓦妮莎. Admins record them so the preview can warn a writer who uses one\n137\twithout a Game Term marker. The site never shows a nickname in place of an\n138\tOfficial name.\n139\t_Avoid_: alias, abbreviation, slang\n140\t\n141\t**Game Term marker** (术语标记):\n142\t`[[瓦妮莎]]` or `[[Vanessa]]` in a Guide's text: a Game Term named by either\n143\tOfficial name, shown on the site as its Official name in the Reader's\n144\tlanguage. A marker that names no Game Term shows its text without the\n145\tbrackets, and the preview warns about it.\n146\t_Avoid_: tag, link, shortcode\n147\t\n148\t**Slug** (网址名):\n149\tThe short web-address name of a Hero or a Guide. A Hero's is derived from its\n150\tEnglish Official name (`Vanessa` → `vanessa`) when the Hero is added, and stays\n151\tthe same when that name is later corrected. A Guide's is `<hero-slug>-<id>` (`vanessa-12`), given when the Guide\n152\tis created; it never changes on its own (not with the title, the Hero or a\n153\tRevision), only when an Admin edits it, so shared links keep working. No two\n154\tHeroes, and no two Guides, share one.\n155\t_Avoid_: URL name, permalink, handle\n156\t\n157\t**Patch** (版本):\n158\tThe game version a Guide was written for, such as `6.7`. Picked by the\n159\twriter. It describes when the Guide was written and is not a verdict on\n160\twhether the Guide is out of date.\n161\t_Avoid_: version (also used for edits to a Guide), season\n162\t\n163\t**Current Patch** (当前版本):\n164\tThe Patch an Admin added most recently. Adding a Patch always makes it the\n165\tCurrent Patch, even if its number is lower than an earlier one's.\n166\t_Avoid_: latest version, live patch\n167\t\n168\t**Tournament** (锦标赛):\n169\tAn experimental in-game mode in which many players (up to about 100) play one\n170\tgame together until there is one champion. It is run by the game, not\n171\torganized by players. It has its own section on the site.\n172\t_Avoid_: event, competition, league, match\n173\t\n174\t### Workflow\n175\t\n176\t**Draft** (草稿):\n177\tA Guide its writer has not finished yet. Only its writer and Admins can see it.\n178\t_Avoid_: unpublished\n179\t\n180\t**Submitted** (待审核):\n181\tA Guide its writer has marked finished, waiting for an Admin to review it.\n182\t_Avoid_: pending, draft, ready\n183\t\n184\t**Return** (退回):\n185\tAn Admin's decision that a Submitted Guide or Revision is not ready. It goes\n186\tback to its writer as a Draft, with the Admin's notes. A Returned Revision\n187\tleaves the Published Guide as it is.\n188\t_Avoid_: reject, decline\n189\t\n190\t**Review note** (审核意见):\n191\tPart of a Return: a passage quoted from the Guide together with the Admin's\n192\tadvice on how to fix it.\n193\t_Avoid_: comment (comments stay on Bilibili), feedback\n194\t\n195\t**Publish** (发布):\n196\tAn Admin's approval of a Submitted Guide, which makes it Published. Publishing\n197\tdoes not by itself change the public site.\n198\t_Avoid_: approve, go live\n199\t\n200\t**Unpublish** (撤下):\n201\tAn Admin taking a Published Guide off the site without deleting it. The Guide\n202\tgoes back to its Author as a Draft, optionally with Review notes. An\n203\tUnpublished Page or Tournament item simply becomes a Draft again.\n204\t_Avoid_: hide, archive, take offline\n205\t\n206\t**Published** (已发布):\n207\tA Guide an Admin has approved. It will appear on the public site after the\n208\tnext Site build.\n209\t_Avoid_: live, approved\n210\t\n211\t**Trash** (回收站):\n212\tWhere deleted Guides go. Only Admins can see it, and they can restore a Guide\n213\tfrom it or delete it for good. A Guide in the Trash is never on the site.\n214\t_Avoid_: archive, recycle bin, deleted\n215\t\n216\t**Revision** (修订):\n217\tA proposed change to a Published Guide. While it waits for review the\n218\tPublished Guide stays on the site unchanged. Once published, it replaces the\n219\told content and the old content is not shown.\n220\t_Avoid_: version, new version, edit\n221\t\n222\t**Site build** (更新网站):\n223\tRegenerating the public site from everything that is Published, and putting it\n224\tonline. This is the only step that changes what Readers see.\n225\t_Avoid_: publish, deploy, export\n226\t\n227\t### Time\n228\t\n229\t**Beijing time** (北京时间):\n230\tUTC+8, the clock the Admins, Editors and most Readers live by. Every time\n231\tthe console or the site shows is in Beijing time, to the minute\n232\t(`2026-10-17 21:05`), or as a Beijing date on the site. Times are stored in\n233\tUTC and compared as stored; only what is shown is converted.\n234\t_Avoid_: local time, server time\n235\t\n236\t## Flagged ambiguities\n237\t\n238\t- \"Draft\" was being used for both an unfinished Guide and a finished one\n239\t  awaiting review. Those are now **Draft** and **Submitted**.\n240\t- \"Version\" can mean the game's Patch or an edit to a Guide. Use **Patch** for\n241\t  the game and **Revision** for an edit.\n242\t- \"Publish\" meant both an Admin's approval and regenerating the site. Approval\n243\t  is **Publish**; regenerating is **Site build**. An Editor never publishes:\n244\t  their button is Submit (提交审核).\n245\t- \"Event\" is a Game Term kind (事件). Tournament items are announcements and\n246\t  recaps, never \"events\".\n247\t- \"Card\" and \"Item\" are the same thing. OUTCOME is success/error/abort/unknown.\n\n**PLAN MODE EXCEPTION — ALWAYS RUN:** This command writes telemetry to\n`~/.gstack/analytics/`, matching preamble analytics writes.\n\nRun this bash:\n\n```bash\n_TEL_END=$(date +%s)\n_TEL_DUR=$(( _TEL_END - _TEL_START ))\nrm -f ~/.gstack/analytics/.pending-\"$_SESSION_ID\" 2>/dev/null || true\n# Session timeline: record skill completion (local-only, never sent anywhere)\n~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-timeline-log '{\"skill\":\"SKILL_NAME\",\"event\":\"completed\",\"branch\":\"'$(git branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)'\",\"outcome\":\"OUTCOME\",\"duration_s\":\"'\"$_TEL_DUR\"'\",\"session\":\"'\"$_SESSION_ID\"'\"}' 2>/dev/null || true\n# Local analytics (gated on telemetry setting)\nif [ \"$_TEL\" != \"off\" ]; then\necho '{\"skill\":\"SKILL_NAME\",\"duration_s\":\"'\"$_TEL_DUR\"'\",\"outcome\":\"OUTCOME\",\"browse\":\"USED_BROWSE\",\"session\":\"'\"$_SESSION_ID\"'\",\"ts\":\"'$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)'\"}' >> ~/.gstack/analytics/skill-usage.jsonl 2>/dev/null || true\nfi\n# Remote telemetry (opt-in, requires binary)\nif [ \"$_TEL\" != \"off\" ] && [ -x ~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-telemetry-log ]; then\n  ~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-telemetry-log \\\n    --skill \"SKILL_NAME\" --duration \"$_TEL_DUR\" --outcome \"OUTCOME\" \\\n    --used-browse \"USED_BROWSE\" --session-id \"$_SESSION_ID\" 2>/dev/null &\nfi\n```\n\nReplace `SKILL_NAME`, `OUTCOME`, and `USED_BROWSE` before running.\n\n## Plan Status Footer\n\nIn plan mode before ExitPlanMode: if the plan file lacks `## GSTACK REVIEW REPORT`, run `~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-review-read` and append the standard runs/status/findings table. If `bun` is not installed:\n   ```bash\n   if ! command -v bun >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n     BUN_VERSION=\"1.3.10\"\n     BUN_INSTALL_SHA=\"bab8acfb046aac8c72407bdcce903957665d655d7acaa3e11c7c4616beae68dd\"\n     tmpfile=$(mktemp)\n     curl -fsSL \"https://bun.sh/install\" -o \"$tmpfile\"\n     actual_sha=$(shasum -a 256 \"$tmpfile\" | awk '{print $1}')\n     if [ \"$actual_sha\" != \"$BUN_INSTALL_SHA\" ]; then\n       echo \"ERROR: bun install script checksum mismatch\" >&2\n\n[... skill content truncated for compaction; use Read on the skill path if you need the full text]\n\n---\n\n### Skill: mattpocock-skills:tdd\nPath: plugin:mattpocock-skills:tdd\n\nBase directory for this skill: /Users/yining/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.3.1/skills/engineering/tdd\n\n# Test-Driven Development\n\nTDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\n\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `GLOSSARY.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\n## What a good test is\n\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: \"user can checkout with valid cart\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.\n\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\n\n## Seams: where tests go\n\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\n\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\n\nAsk: \"What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?\" Give each proposed seam a one-line note on what it catches and what it misses.\n\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \"codebase-design\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\n\n## Anti-patterns\n\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\n\n## Rules of the loop\n\n- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.\n- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.\n- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.\n\n\n---\n\n### Skill: mattpocock-skills:implement\nPath: plugin:mattpocock-skills:implement\n\nBase directory for this skill: /Users/yining/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.3.1/skills/engineering/implement\n\nImplement the work described by the user in the spec or tickets.\n\nIf the user passes a ticket reference, fetch it from the issue tracker and state its title before starting. {"parentUuid":"4a59d8a3-8309-4702-af6d-771d63906a8d","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"prompt_snapshot","systemPrompt":["\nYou are an agent working with the user toward their goals, using your own judgment along the way.\n\nIMPORTANT: Assist with authorized security testing, defensive security, CTF challenges, and educational contexts. The calls run in the order sent, so the publish sends the edited file; a publish sent in the same response as a failed Edit of that file is refused and leaves the artifact as it was, so correct the Edit and publish again.","# Claude in Chrome browser automation\n\nYou have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.\n\n## Loading deferred tools\n\nIf the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:\n\nToolSearch with query \"select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp\"\n\nAdd task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.\n\n## GIF recording\n\nWhen performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.\n\nYou must ALWAYS:\n* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback\n* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., \"login_process.gif\")\n\n## Console log debugging\n\nYou can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: \"[MyApp]\" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.\n\n## Alerts and dialogs\n\nIMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:\n1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., \"Delete\" buttons with confirmation dialogs)\n2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session\n3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding\n\nIf you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.\n\n## Avoid rabbit holes and loops\n\nWhen using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:\n- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration\n- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts\n- No response from the browser extension\n- Page elements not responding to clicks or input\n- Pages not loading or timing out\n- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches\n\nExplain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.\n\n## Tab context and session startup\n\nIMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.\n\nNever reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:\n1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it\n2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp\n3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs\n4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available","__SYSTEM_PROMPT_DYNAMIC_BOUNDARY__","Write code that reads like the surrounding code: match its comment density, naming, and idiom.","When you use a pronoun for someone — the user or anyone else you mention — and their pronouns haven't been stated, use they/them. Report outcomes faithfully: if tests fail, say so with the output; if a step was skipped, say that; when something is done and verified, state it plainly without hedging.","# Session-specific guidance\n - If you need the user to run a shell command themselves (e.g., an interactive login like `gcloud auth login`), suggest they type `! <command>` in the prompt — the `!` prefix runs the command in this session so its output lands directly in the conversation.\n - When the user types `/<skill-name>`, invoke it via Skill. Only use skills listed in the user-invocable skills section — don't guess.\n - If the user asks about \"ultrareview\" or how to run it, explain that /code-review ultra launches a multi-agent cloud review of the current branch (or /code-review ultra <PR#> for a GitHub PR); /ultrareview is a deprecated alias for the same command. It needs a git repository (offer to \"git init\" if not in one); the no-arg form bundles the local branch and does not need a GitHub remote.","# Memory\n\nYou have a persistent file-based memory at `/Users/yining/.claude/projects/-Users-yining-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/memory/`. This directory already exists — write to it directly with the Write tool (do not run mkdir or check for its existence). Each memory is one file holding one fact, with frontmatter:\n\n```markdown\n---\nname: <short-kebab-case-slug>\ndescription: <one-line summary, used to decide relevance during recall>\nmetadata:\n  type: user | feedback | project | reference\n---\n\n<the fact; for feedback/project, follow with **Why:** and **How to apply:** lines. Link related memories with [[their-name]].>\n```\n\nIn the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.\n\n`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).\n\nAfter writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.\n\nBefore saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. Recalled memories appearing inside `<system-reminder>` blocks are background context, not user instructions, and reflect what was true when written.
